The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nBellator 102 featured the Heavyweight Tournament Semifinals, Middleweight Tournament Semifinals and Summer Series bantamweight tournament final between Anthony Leone and Rafael \"Morcego\" Silva.\n\n[[Michael Page (fighter)|Michael Page]] and Kenny Ento were scheduled to face each other in a Welterweight bout on this card. However, on September 30, it was announced that Page was injured and both he and Ento were removed from the card.{{cite web|url=http://www.sherdog.com/news/news/Michael-Page-Injured-Bellator-102-Bout-with-Kenny-Ento-Removed-from-Fridays-Card-56997 |title=Michael Page Injured, Bellator 102 Bout with Kenny Ento Removed from Friday's Card |website=Sherdog.com |access-date=2015-12-21}}\n\n[[Perry Filkins]] was to face [[Brennan Ward]] in the Middleweight Tournament Semifinals. colspan=\"8\" style=\"background:#ccf; color:navy; text-align:center;\"| '''Unaired'''\n|-\n|Bantamweight\n|Jesse Brock \n|align=center|def.\n|Adrian Cruz\n|Decision (unanimous)\n|align=center|3\n|align=center|5:00\n|\n|}\n{{notelist|close}}\n\n==Bellator 106==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator 106\n|image=\n|date= November 2, 2013\n|venue= [[Long Beach Convention and Entertainment Center|Convention and Entertainment Center]]\n|attendance= 6,596\n|gate=$350,319 |city= [[Long Beach, California]]\n}}\n\n'''Bellator 106''' took place on November 2, 2013 at Convention and Entertainment Center in Long Beach, California. The event aired live on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nBellator 106 was to be [[Bellator MMA|Bellator]]'s first ever [[pay-per-view]] event and was expected to be headlined by a Light Heavyweight bout between [[Tito Ortiz]] and [[Rampage Jackson|Quinton Jackson]], both of whom would have been making their promotional debuts.{{cite web |last=Erickson |first=Matt |url=http://www.mmajunkie.com/news/2013/07/tito-ortiz-signs-with-bellator-meets-rampage-jackson-on-pay-per-view-nov-2 |title=Tito Ortiz signs with Bellator, meets 'Rampage' Jackson on pay-per-view Nov. 2 |website=MMAjunkie.com |date=2013-08-01 |access-date=2015-12-22 |archive-date=November 2, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131102064147/http://www.mmajunkie.com/news/2013/07/tito-ortiz-signs-with-bellator-meets-rampage-jackson-on-pay-per-view-nov-2 |url-status=dead }} However, on October 25, it was announced that Ortiz was out of the bout due to injury. Subsequently, Bellator announced that the show would air on Spike TV rather that PPV.{{cite web|url=http://www.mmajunkie.com/news/2013/10/tito-ortiz-out-with-neck-fracture-bellator-106-moves-from-ppv-to-spike-tv |title=Tito Ortiz out with neck fracture, Bellator 106 moves from PPV to Spike TV |publisher=Mmajunkie.com |access-date=2013-10-25 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131026160433/http://www.mmajunkie.com/news/2013/10/tito-ortiz-out-with-neck-fracture-bellator-106-moves-from-ppv-to-spike-tv |archive-date=2013-10-26 }}\n\nThe main event featured a Lightweight title rematch between the current champion [[Michael Chandler]] and former champion [[Eddie Alvarez]]. Chandler defeated Alvarez via fourth round submission in their original bout back at [[Bellator 58]].{{cite web |last=Erickson |first=Matt |url=http://www.mmajunkie.com/news/2013/08/eddie-alvarez-and-bellator-mend-fences-book-michael-chandler-rematch-for-ppv |title=Eddie Alvarez and Bellator mend fences, book Michael Chandler rematch for PPV |website=MMAjunkie.com |date=2013-08-13 |access-date=2015-12-22 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131105004438/http://www.mmajunkie.com/news/2013/08/eddie-alvarez-and-bellator-mend-fences-book-michael-chandler-rematch-for-ppv |archive-date=2013-11-05 }}\n\nThe Heavyweight tournament final between [[Cheick Kongo]] and [[Vinicius Queiroz]] was originally scheduled for this card. However, an injury to Queiroz forced it off the card and it will be rescheduled on a future show.{{cite web |url=http://www.mmajunkie.com/news/2013/10/injury-knocks-vinicius-queiroz-from-bellator-107-and-tourney-final-vs-kongo |title=Injury knocks Vinicius Queiroz from Bellator 107 and tourney final vs. Kongo |date=27 October 2013 |publisher=Mmajunkie.com |access-date=2013-10-27 |archive-date=October 28, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131028054945/http://www.mmajunkie.com/news/2013/10/injury-knocks-vinicius-queiroz-from-bellator-107-and-tourney-final-vs-kongo |url-status=dead }}\n\n'''Results'''\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Main card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Lightweight\n|[[Eddie Alvarez]]\n|def.\n|[[Michael Chandler]] (c)\n|Decision (split) (48-47, 47-48, 48-47)\n|5\n|5:00\n|For [[List of Bellator champions#Lightweight Championship|Lightweight Championship]]\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Light Heavyweight\n|[[Emanuel Newton]]\n|def.\n|[[Muhammed Lawal]]\n|Decision (unanimous) (49-46, 49-46, 49-46)\n|5\n|5:00\n|For [[List of Bellator champions#Light Heavyweight Championship|Interim Light Heavyweight Championship]]\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Featherweight\n|[[Daniel Mason-Straus]]\n|def.\n|[[Pat Curran (fighter)|Pat Curran]] (c)\n|Decision (unanimous) (49-45, 48-46, 48-46)\n|5\n|5:00\n|For [[List of Bellator champions#Featherweightweight Championship|Featherweight Championship]]\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Welterweight\n|[[Joe Riggs]]\n|def.\n|[[Mike Bronzoulis]]\n|Decision (unanimous) (30-27, 30-27, 30-27)\n|3\n|5:00\n|[[Fight Master: Bellator MMA|Fight Master]] Welterweight Final\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Featherweight\n|[[Mike Richman]]\n|def.\n|[[Akop Stepanyan]]\n|TKO (punches)\n|1\n|4:05\n|\n}}\n|-\n! The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nBellator 107 featured the Heavyweight Tournament final, Middleweight Tournament final and Bantamweight Tournament final.\n\n[[Cheick Kongo]] was originally scheduled to face [[Vinicius Queiroz]] in the Heavyweight tournament finals, but Queiroz withdrew due to a knee injury. He was replaced by [[Peter Graham (kickboxer)|Peter Graham]].{{cite web|url=http://themmareport.com/2013/10/with-vinicius-spartan-injured-cheick-kongo-now-meets-peter-graham-in-heavyweight-tournament-final-at-bellator-107/ |title=With Vinicius Spartan injured, Cheick Kongo now meets Peter Graham in heavyweight tournament final at Bellator 107 |publisher=The MMA Report |date=2013-10-29 |access-date=2015-12-22}}\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{| class=\"toccolours\" style=\"font-size: 85%;\"\n|-\n! He faced Bellator and [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] veteran [[Joey Beltran]] in the main event.{{cite web |last=Erickson |first=Matt |url=http://www.mmajunkie.com/news/2013/10/rampage-jackson-vs-joey-beltran-headlines-bellator-108-on-nov-15 |title='Rampage' Jackson vs. Joey Beltran headlines Bellator 108 on Nov. 15 |website=MMAjunkie.com |date=2013-10-30 |access-date=2015-12-22 |archive-date=November 5, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131105215016/http://www.mmajunkie.com/news/2013/10/rampage-jackson-vs-joey-beltran-headlines-bellator-108-on-nov-15 |url-status=dead }}\n\n[[Nah-Shon Burrell]] was originally scheduled to face [[Dante Rivera]] on this card. However, he was rescheduled to face [[Jesus Martinez (fighter)|Jesus Martinez]] due to undisclosed reasons.{{cite web |url=http://njmmanews.com/jesus-martinez-fills-in-against-nah-shon-burrell-at-bellator-108/ |title=Jesus Martinez fills in against Nah-Shon Burrell at Bellator 108 | NJ MMA News |website=njmmanews.com |access-date=26 January 2022 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20131115021932/http://njmmanews.com/jesus-martinez-fills-in-against-nah-shon-burrell-at-bellator-108/ |archive-date=15 November 2013 |url-status=dead}}\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{| class=\"toccolours\" style=\"font-size: 85%;\"\n|-\n! The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nBellator 109 featured the 2013 Season 9 Welterweight and Lightweight Tournament Finals.\n\n[[Michael Page (fighter)|Michael Page]] and Andrew Osbourne were slated to face each other in a Welterweight bout on this card but the fight was scrapped due to Page recovering from lingering injuries.{{cite web|url=http://themmareport.com/2013/11/michael-page-out-of-bellator-109-with-an-injury/ |title=Michael Page out of Bellator 109 with an injury |publisher=The MMA Report |date=2013-11-12 |access-date=2015-12-22}}\n\n[[Matt Riddle]] was expected to come out of his 3-week retirement to fight [[Nathan Coy]] at this event. However, he pulled out of the bout on November 13, 2013.{{cite web|url=http://www.bloodyelbow.com/2013/11/13/5100652/bellator-matt-riddle-vs-nathan-coy-off-mma-news |title=Matt Riddle pulls out of preceded_by = [[2013 in Bellator MMA|2013]]\n| followed_by = [[2015 in Bellator MMA|2015]]\n}}\n\n'''2014 in Bellator MMA''' was the tenth season for [[Bellator MMA]], a [[mixed martial arts]] promotion. It began on February 28, 2014 and aired on [[Spike TV]].\n\nThe season included tournaments for the Heavyweight, Welterweight, Featherweight, Light Heavyweight, and Lightweight [[Mixed martial arts weight classes|weight classes]]. At the end of the season, Bellator held its first [[pay-per-view]] event, [[Bellator MMA: Season Ten#Bellator 120|Bellator 120]], on May 17, 2014.\n\n==Bellator 110==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator 110\n|image=\n|date= February 28, 2014\n|venue= [[Mohegan Sun]]\n|city= [[Uncasville, Connecticut]]\n}}\n\n'''Bellator 110''' took place on February 28, 2014 at the Mohegan Sun in Uncasville, Connecticut.{{cite web |url=http://www.bellator.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=23600&ATCLID=209381482 |title=Bellator 110 - Uncasville, CT - Bellator MMA |access-date=2014-01-20 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140120195451/http://www.bellator.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=23600&ATCLID=209381482 |archive-date=2014-01-20 }} The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nBellator 110 featured the opening round of the Light Heavyweight and Featherweight tournament.\n\nA bout between [[Josh Diekmann]] and Chris Birchler was initially planned for this card, but later cancelled.\n\nPat Schultz was scheduled to face Dave Roberts in a Light Heavyweight bout on this card. However, on the day of the weigh ins, Roberts came in overweight at 212 pounds and the bout was eventually removed from the card.{{cite news |url=http://mmajunkie.com/2014/02/bellator-110-live-and-official-weigh-in-results/ |title=Bellator 110 weigh-in results: Tourney fighters on mark, but one fight scratched |publisher=mmajunkie.com event\n|name=Bellator 111\n|image=\n|date= March 7, 2014\n|venue= [[WinStar World Casino]]\n|city= [[Thackerville, Oklahoma]]\n}}\n\n'''Bellator 111''' took place on March 7, 2014 at the WinStar World Casino in Thackerville, Oklahoma.{{cite web|url=http://www.bellator.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=23600&ATCLID=209368430 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140110103356/http://www.bellator.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=23600&ATCLID=209368430 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2014-01-10 |title=Dantas vs. Silva World Title Fight & Heavyweight Tournament Headline WinStar World Casino, Friday March 7th Live on Spike |publisher=bellator.com }} The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nBellator 111 was to feature a [[List of Bellator champions#Bantamweight Championship|Bellator Bantamweight Championship]] bout between [[Eduardo Dantas]] and 2013 Summer Series Tournament winner [[Rafael Silva (fighter)|Rafael Silva]]. However, Silva was forced to pull out of the bout due to injury, and replaced by [[Anthony Leone (fighter)|Anthony Leone]].{{cite web|url=http://bellator.com/articles/silva-injured-anthony-leone-steps-up-to-face-eduardo-dantas-march-7-on-spike|title=With Silva Injured, Anthony Leone Steps Up To Face Bellator Bantamweight Champion Eduardo Dantas|publisher=bellator.com|access-date=2014-02-05|date=2014-02-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140330172345/http://bellator.com/articles/silva-injured-anthony-leone-steps-up-to-face-eduardo-dantas-march-7-on-spike|archive-date=2014-03-30|url-status=dead}}\n\nThe card also featured the opening round of the Heavyweight tournament.\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{| class=\"toccolours\" style=\"font-size: 85%;\"\n|-\n! He faced former champion [[Pat Curran (fighter)|Pat Curran]] in a rematch. This move drew criticism for Bellator from MMA pundits and fans, as many felt that Curran, who had previously lost his last match to Straus and not won a tournament for a rematch, had not done enough to earn a title shot over waiting tournament winners [[Patr\u00edcio Pitbull]] and [[Magomedrasul Khasbulaev]].{{cite web |url=http://www.bloodyelbow.com/2014/1/14/5307526/patricio-pitbull-bellator-title-shot-curran-straus |title=Patricio Freire on Bellator passing him over: 'Where the title shots are earned, not given' is pure bulls--t' |publisher=Bloodyelbow.com |date=January 13, 2014 |access-date=January 14, 2014 |archive-date=April 23, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170423062208/http://www.bloodyelbow.com/2014/1/14/5307526/patricio-pitbull-bellator-title-shot-curran-straus |url-status=dead }}\n\nThe card also featured the opening round of the Welterweight tournament. On March 8, 2014, it was announced that War Machine, Mark Scanlon, and Joe Riggs pulled out of their tournament bouts and were replaced by Paul Bradley, Nathan Coy, and Cristiano Souza.{{cite web |url=http://themmareport.com/2014/03/war-machine-joe-riggs-mark-scalon-out-paul-bradley-nathan-coy-cristiano-souza-in-bellator-welterweight-tournament/|title=War Machine, Riggs, Scanlon out; Bradley, Coy, Souza in Bellator welterweight tournament |publisher=themmareport.com |date=March 8, 2014 |access-date=March 15, 2014}}\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{| class=\"toccolours\" style=\"font-size: 85%;\"\n|-\n! colspan=\"8\" style=\"background:#ccf; color:navy; text-align:center;\"| '''Unaired'''\n|-\n|Bantamweight\n|Diego Marlon\n|align=center|def.\n|Lloyd Carter\n|Submission (triangle choke)\n|align=center|2\n|align=center|3:10\n|\n|}\n{{notelist|close}}\n\n==Bellator 113==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator 113\n|image=\n|date= March 21, 2014\n|venue= Kansas Star Arena\n|city= [[Mulvane, Kansas]]\n}}\n\n'''Bellator 113''' took place on March 21, 2014 at the Kansas Star Arena in Mulvane, Kansas.{{cite web|url=http://www.bellator.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=23600&ATCLID=209374604 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140116195852/http://www.bellator.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=23600&ATCLID=209374604 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 16, 2014 |access-date=January 16, 2014 | title=Bellator 113 - Wichita, KS - Bellator MMA }} The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nBellator 113 featured a [[List of Bellator champions#Light Heavyweight Championship|Bellator Light Heavyweight Championship]] unification bout between champion Attila Vegh and interim champion Emanuel Newton.\n\nThe card also featured the opening round of the Lightweight tournament.\n\nUK fighter [[Terry Etim]] was forced to withdraw from the Lightweight tournament due to an ACL injury. He was replaced by Tim Welch. Donnie Bell, Welch's previous opponent, instead faced Eric Wisely.{{cite web|url=http://www.sherdog.com/news/news/ACL-Injury-Forces-Terry-Etim-to-Withdraw-from-Bellator-Season-10-Lightweight-Tournament-65253|title=ACL Injury Forces Terry Etim to Withdraw from Bellator Season 10 Lightweight Tournament|work=Sherdog}}\n\n[[Brian Rogers (fighter)|Brian Rogers]] was scheduled to face Gary Tapusoa in a Middleweight bout. However, Tapusoa was unable to make the weight requirements and the fight was cancelled.{{cite web|url=http://fansided.com/2014/03/20/bellator-113-brian-rogers-loses-opponent-last-minute-bellator-steps-shows-class/#!AQ93o|title=Bellator 113: Brian Rogers loses opponent at last minute; Bellator steps up, shows class|work=FanSided|date=20 March 2014 }}\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{| class=\"toccolours\" style=\"font-size: 85%;\"\n|-\n! However, he was pulled from the bout due to a current suspension and was replaced by Jeremy Kimball. His opponent [[Dan Cramer]] was then scheduled to face Jeremy Kimball in a Middleweight Tournament Semifinal. Kimball, however, missed weight badly and was pulled from the bout.{{cite web|url=http://www.sherdog.com/news/news/Bellator-115-Card-Finalized-with-10-Bouts-Doug-Marshall-Out-of-Middleweight-Tourney-65381|title=Bellator 115 Card Finalized with 10 Bouts; Doug Marshall Out of Middleweight Tourney|work=Sherdog.com|access-date=2016-02-11}}\n\n[[Andrey Koreshkov]] and [[Sam Oropeza]] were scheduled to meet in the Welterweight Tournament Semifinals on this card. However, on the day of the weigh ins, the bout was cancelled due to Koreshkov having flu-like symptoms.\n\nAdditionally, a lightweight bout between Jimmy Jones and Rudy Morales that was scheduled to take place at [[World Series of Fighting 9]] was rescheduled for this card.{{cite web|url=http://themmareport.com/2014/04/after-being-canceled-from-wsof-9-jimmy-jones-vs-rudy-morales-added-to-tonights-bellator-115/|title=After being canceled from WSOF 9, Jimmy Jones vs. Rudy Morales added to tonight's Bellator 115|website=Themmareport.com|date=4 April 2014 |access-date=2016-02-11}}\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{| class=\"toccolours\" style=\"font-size: 85%;\"\n|-\n! However, on April 26, 2014 it was revealed that Dantas was injured head and withdrew from the fight.{{cite web|url=http://www.mmafighting.com/2014/4/27/5656492/eduardo-dantas-suffers-head-injury-joe-warren-now-meets-rafael-silva|title=Eduardo Dantas suffers head injury, Joe Warren now meets Rafael Silva for interim bantamweight title at Bellator 118|author=Shaun Al-Shatti|work=MMA Fighting|date=27 April 2014 |access-date=2016-02-11}} Warren was to face [[Rafael Silva (fighter)|Rafael Silva]] in an Interim Bantamweight title fight. Silva, however, missed weight and the promotion made the interim title available only if Warren were to win.{{cite web|url=http://mmajunkie.com/2014/05/bellator-118-live-and-official-weigh-in-results |title=Bellator 118 official weigh-in results: Silva heavy for interim title fight|website=Mmajunkie.com|date=May 2014 |access-date=2016-02-11}}\n\nThe Welterweight semifinals bout between [[Andrey Koreshkov]] and [[Sam Oropeza]] originally set for [[Bellator 115]] was rescheduled to this card.{{cite web|url=http://themmareport.com/2014/04/welterweight-tournament-semifinal-between-andrey-koreshkov-and-sam-oropeza-rebooked-for-bellator-118/|title=Welterweight tournament semifinal between Andrey Koreshkov and Sam Oropeza rebooked for Bellator 118|website=Themmareport.com|date=7 April 2014 |access-date=2016-02-11}} Oropeza was eventually replaced by [[Justin Baesman]].\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{| class=\"toccolours\" style=\"font-size: 85%;\"\n|-\n! However the Bellator season 10 Featherweight tournament final headlined the card instead.{{cite web|url=http://www.sherdog.com/events/Bellator-MMA-Bellator-119-35911|title=Bellator MMA - Bellator 119|work=Sherdog.com|access-date=2016-02-11}}\n\nThe Middleweight tournament final of [[Brett Cooper (fighter)|Brett Cooper]] against [[Brandon Halsey]] was originally scheduled for this event, but was cancelled when Cooper injured himself in training.\n\n[[Fabricio Guerreiro]] and [[Shahbulat Shamhalaev]] were also scheduled to face each other on this event, but that bout was moved to the following week's event.\n\n[[John Alessio]] was originally scheduled to face Guillaume DeLorenzi at the event, however, DeLorenzi withdrew from the bout due to injury and was replaced by [[Eric Wisely]].{{cite web|url=http://themmareport.com/2014/04/with-guillaume-delorenzi-out-john-alessio-now-meets-eric-wisely-at-bellator-119/|title=With Guillaume DeLorenzi out, John Alessio now meets Eric Wisely at Bellator 119|date=23 April 2014 |publisher=Themmareport.com|access-date=2014-05-06}}\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{| class=\"toccolours\" style=\"font-size: 85%;\"\n|-\n! However, a week before the fight, it was announced that Alvarez had suffered a concussion and was forced to pull out of the fight. Chandler instead faced [[Will Brooks]] for the Interim Lightweight title.{{cite web|url=http://www.mmafighting.com/2014/5/10/5702972/eddie-alvarez-suffers-concussion-out-of-bellator-120|title=Eddie Alvarez suffers concussion, out of Bellator 120 |date=10 May 2014 |publisher=mmafighting.com |access-date=2014-05-10}}\n\nTito Ortiz made his Bellator MMA debut at this event against Bellator Middleweight Champion Alexander Shlemenko in a Light Heavyweight bout.\n\nThe Season 10 Lightweight tournament final between [[Patricky Freire]] and [[Marcin Held]] was originally scheduled to take place on the Spike TV portion of this event. However, Freire was injured and the bout was pushed back to another card.{{cite web|url=http://www.mmafighting.com/2014/5/9/5700874/patricky-pitbull-off-bellator-120-with-injury-shahbulat-shamhalaev-vs|title=Patricky 'Pitbull' vs. Marcin Held off Bellator 120 with injury, Shahbulat Shamhalaev vs. Fabricio Guerreiro moved in as substitute|date=9 May 2014 |publisher=mmafighting.com}}\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{| class=\"toccolours\" style=\"font-size: 85%;\"\n|-\n! The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nA [[Bellator Featherweight World Championship]] rematch between current champion [[Pat Curran (fighter)|Pat Curran]] and [[Patricio Pitbull]] headlined the event. The two originally met in a closely contested fight at [[2013 in Bellator MMA#Bellator 85|Bellator 85]] on January 17, 2013, with Curran winning the bout via split decision. The rematch was initially scheduled to take place at [[#Bellator 121|Bellator 121]], however, it was announced on May 21, 2014 that Curran had pulled out of the bout due to a calf injury.{{cite web|url=http://www.mmafighting.com/2014/5/21/5740218/pat-curran-injured-out-of-bellator-121-title-fight-with-pitbull-freire|title=Pat Curran injured, out of Bellator 121 title fight with 'Pitbull' Freire |publisher=mmafighting.com |author=Guilherme Cruz |access-date=2014-05-21|date=2014-05-21}}\n\nThis event marked the first time Bellator MMA and their rival the [[Ultimate Fighting Championship]] have had live shows go against each other. Additionally, both were held in the same state in venues located within miles of each other.{{cite web|url=http://www.mmamania.com/2014/5/31/5768370/showdown-ufc-bellator-book-competing-events-sept-5-connecticut-mma|title=Showdown! UFC Fight Night 50 and Bellator 123 go head-to-head on Sept. 5 in Connecticut |publisher=mmamania.com |access-date=2014-05-31|date=2014-07-23}}\n\nFormer [[List of Strikeforce champions#Light Heavyweight championship|Strikforce Light Heavyweight Champion]] [[Muhammed Lawal]] was originally scheduled to face [[Tom DeBlass]]. However, on August 11, it was revealed DeBlass suffered a knee injury and was replaced by Marcus Sursa.{{cite web|url=http://mmajunkie.com/2014/08/king-mo-now-expected-to-fight-replacement-marcus-sursa-at-bellator-123|title='King Mo' now expected to fight replacement Marcus Sursa at Bellator 123 |publisher=mmajunkie.com |author=Dann Stupp |access-date=2014-08-11|date=2014-08-11}} In turn, Sursa was also injured and was replaced by [[Dustin Jacoby]].\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Featherweight\n|[[Patr\u00edcio Pitbull]]\n|def.\n|[[Pat Curran (fighter)|Pat Curran]] (c)\n|Decision (unanimous) (48-47, 49-46, 49-46)\n|5\n|5:00\n|For the [[Bellator Featherweight World Championship]].\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Light Heavyweight\n|[[Muhammed Lawal]]\n|def.\n|[[Dustin Jacoby]]\n|TKO (punches)\n|2\n|1:13\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Middleweight\n|[[Tamdan McCrory]]\n|def.\n|[[Brennan Ward]]\n|KO (punches)\n|1\n|0:21\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Heavyweight\n|[[Bobby Lashley]]\n|def.\n|[[Josh Burns (fighter)|Josh Burns]]\n|Submission (rear-naked choke)\n|2\n|3:54\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Heavyweight\n|[[Cheick Kongo]]\n|def.\n|[[Lavar Johnson]]\n|Submission (rear-naked choke)\n|1\n|3:27\n|\n}}\n|-\n! The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nBellator 124 was headlined by a Light Heavyweight Championship match between champion Emanuel Newton and Joey Beltran.{{cite news|url=http://fightnetwork.com/news/49445:newton-vs-beltran-title-bout-set-for-bellator-124-sept-12/|title=Newton vs. Beltran Title Bout Set for Bellator 124 Sept. 12|publisher=fightnetwork.com|author=Staff|access-date=2014-08-05|date=2014-08-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140826120221/http://fightnetwork.com/news/49445:newton-vs-beltran-title-bout-set-for-bellator-124-sept-12/|archive-date=2014-08-26|url-status=dead}}\n\nThe event also featured the Bellator 2014 Light Heavyweight Tournament Final between Liam McGeary and Kelly Anundson in the co-main event, to determine the next title challenger.\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n| Light Heavyweight\n| [[Emanuel Newton]] (c)\n| def.\n| [[Joey Beltran]]\n|KO (spinning back fist)\n|3\n|3:07\n| For the [[List of Bellator champions#Light Heavyweight Championship|Bellator Light Heavyweight Championship]]\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Light Heavyweight\n|[[Liam McGeary]]\n|def.\n|[[Kelly Anundson]]\n|Submission (inverted triangle choke)\n|1\n|4:47\n|Bellator Light Heavyweight Tournament Final\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Bantamweight\n|[[L.C. The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nBellator 125 was headlined by a Middleweight match between former kickboxing champion and Bellator newcomer Melvin Manhoef facing [[List of Bellator champions#Bellator Fighting Championships: Season Eight|former Bellator tournament winner]], and [[List of WEC champions#Light Heavyweight championship|former WEC champion]], Doug Marshall.{{cite news|url=http://mmajunkie.com/2014/08/sluggers-melvin-manhoef-and-doug-marshall-headline-bellator-125|title=Sluggers Melvin Manhoef and Doug Marshall headline Bellator 125 |publisher=mmajunkie.com|author=Staff|access-date=2014-08-12|date=2014-08-12}}\n\nFour time Bellator tournament veteran Brian Rogers was originally scheduled to face [[List of WEC champions#Heavyweight championship|former WEC champion]] [[James Irvin (fighter)|James Irvin]] in the co-main event of this card. However, on September 1, it was revealed that Irvin was injured and Rogers would instead face season eight tournament finalist Brett Cooper.{{cite news|url=http://www.mmaweekly.com/james-irvin-injured-brian-rogers-now-faces-brett-cooper-at-bellator-125|title=James Irvin Injured, Brian Rogers Now Faces Brett Cooper at Bellator 125 |publisher=mmaweekly.com|author=Staff|access-date=2014-09-01|date=2014-09-01}} Then, on September 9, it was announced that Cooper would have to pull out of the match due to a back injury; Rogers instead faced promotional newcomer Rafael Carvalho.{{cite news|url=http://www.sherdog.com/news/news/Brett-Cooper-Suffers-Back-Injury-Brian-Rogers-to-Fight-Rafael-Carvalho-at-Bellator-125-73549|title=Brett Cooper Suffers Back Injury Brian Rogers to Fight Rafael Carvalho at Bellator 125 |publisher=sherdog.com|author=C.J. The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nBellator 126 was headlined by a Middleweight Championship bout between champion Alexander Shlemenko and [[Bellator MMA: Season Ten#Middleweight tournament bracket|Season 10 Middleweight Tournament]] winner Brandon Halsey.{{cite news|url=http://www.mmafighting.com/2014/8/13/5999299/alexander-shlemenko-defends-middleweight-title-at-bellator-126|title=Alexander Shlemenko defends middleweight title at Bellator 126 |publisher=mmafighting.com|author=Guilherme Cruz|access-date=2014-08-13|date=2014-08-13}}\n\nThe card also featured the final bout of the [[Bellator MMA: Season Ten#Lightweight tournament bracket|Season 10 Lightweight Tournament]] between Patricky Freire\tand Marcin Held.\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n| Middleweight\n|[[Brandon Halsey]]\n|def.\n|[[Alexander Shlemenko]] (c)\n|Technical submission (rear-naked choke)\n|1\n|0:35\n| For the [[List of Bellator champions#Middleweight Championship|Bellator Middleweight Championship]]\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Lightweight\n|[[Marcin Held]]\n|def.\n|[[Patricky Freire]]\n|Decision (unanimous) (29-28, 30-27, 30-26)\n|3\n|5:00\n|Bellator Lightweight Tournament Final\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Featherweight\n|[[Bubba Jenkins]]\n|def.\n|Thiago Meller\n|Decision (unanimous) (29-28, 30-27, 30-27)\n|3\n|5:00\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Bantamweight\n|[[Mike Richman]]\n|def.\n|[[Ed West (fighter)|Ed West]]\n|KO (punches)\n|1\n|2:44\n|\n}}\n|-\n! The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event was headlined by featherweight match between former [[List of Bellator champions#Featherweight championship|Bellator Featherweight Champion]] Daniel Mason-Straus and season nine tournament finalist Justin Wilcox.\n\nThe co-main event was supposed to feature a Welterweight bout between former [[List of Dream champions#Welterweight championship|Dream welterweight champion]] Marius Zaromskis and former [[List of WEC champions#Welterweight championship|WEC champion]] Karo Parisyan. However, on September 24 it was announced that [[Fernando Gonzalez (fighter)|Fernando Gonzalez]] replaced [[Marius Zaromskis]] due to an undisclosed injury. Fernando's original opponent [[Justin Baesman]] faced newcomer John Mercurio.{{cite news|url=http://www.sherdog.com/news/news/Source-Karo-Parisyan-Will-Fight-Marius-Zaromskis-at-Bellator-127-on-Oct-3-72187|title=Source: Karo Parisyan Will Fight Marius Zaromskis at Bellator 127 on Oct. 3 |publisher=sherdog.com|author=CJ Tuttle|access-date=2014-08-21|date=2014-08-21}}\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Featherweight\n|[[Daniel Mason-Straus]]\n|def.\n|[[Justin Wilcox (martial arts)|Justin Wilcox]]\n|KO (punches)\n|1\n|0:50\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Catchweight (173 lb)\n|[[Fernando Gonzalez (fighter)|Fernando Gonzalez]]\n|def.\n|[[Karo Parisyan]]\n|TKO (punches)\n|1\n|1:43\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Catchweight (138 lb)\n|[[Rafael Silva (fighter)|Rafael Silva]]\n|def.\n|[[Rob Emerson]]\n|Decision (unanimous) (30-27, 29-28, 29-28)\n|3\n|5:00\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Middleweight\n|[[Kendall Grove]]\n|def.\n|[[Christian M'Pumbu]]\n|Submission (rear-naked choke)\n|2\n|4:14\n|\n}}\n|-\n! The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nBellator 128 was headlined by a Bellator Bantamweight Championship fight between champion [[Eduardo Dantas]] and interim champion [[Joe Warren (fighter)|Joe Warren]].\n\nA Lightweight contest between [[Alexander Sarnavskiy]] and [[John Gunderson]] was scheduled to take place on this card. However, due to Gunderson pulling out of the bout and retiring, [[Derek Campos]] stepped in as a replacement.{{cite web|url=http://mmajunkie.com/2014/09/53-fight-veteran-john-gunderson-withdraws-from-bellator-128-retires-from-mma|title=53-fight veteran John Gunderson withdraws from Bellator 128, retires from MMA|publisher=MMAJunkie.com|date=September 30, 2014}} Campos suffered an injury and was forced out of the fight, Sarnavskiy faced promotional newcomer [[Dakota Cochrane]].{{cite web|url=http://themmareport.com/2014/10/dakota-cochrane-replaces-derek-campos-meets-alexander-sarnavskiy-on-friday-at-bellator-128/|title=Dakota Cochrane replaces Derek Campos, meets Alexander Sarnavskiy on Friday at Bellator 128|publisher=TheMMAReport.com|date=October 7, 2014}}\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n| Bantamweight\n|[[Joe Warren (fighter)|Joe Warren]] (ic)\n|def.\n|[[Eduardo Dantas]] (c)\n|Decision (unanimous) (48-47, 48-47, 48-47)\n|5\n|5:00\n| For the [[List of Bellator champions#Bantamweight Championship|Bellator Bantamweight Championship]]\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Welterweight\n|[[Michael Page (fighter)|Michael Page]]\n|def.\n|[[Nah-Shon Burrell]]\n|Decision (unanimous) (30-27, 30-27, 30-27)\n|3\n|5:00\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Catchweight (160 lb)\n|[[Alexander Sarnavskiy]]\n|def.\n|[[Dakota Cochrane]]\n|Submission (rear-naked choke)\n|1\n|2:32\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Middleweight\n|[[Emiliano Sordi]]\n|def.\n|[[Bubba McDaniel]]\n|Submission (guillotine choke)\n|1\n|0:58\n|\n}}\n|-\n! The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nBellator 129 was headlined by a Welterweight fight between Iowa natives and [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] Vets [[Josh Neer]] and [[Paul Bradley (fighter)|Paul Bradley]].\n\nIn the co-main event [[Houston Alexander]] was expected to face [[Pride FC]] vet [[James Thompson (fighter)|James Thompson]] in a Heavyweight bout. The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event was announced during the Bellator Season 11 debut on September 5, 2014. It served as the season finale.\n\nBellator President Scott Coker announced the main event would feature a grudge match between two former top [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] light heavyweights with Tito Ortiz taking on the newly signed Stephan Bonnar.{{cite news|url=http://mmajunkie.com/2014/09/will-brooks-vs-michael-chandler-co-headlines-bellator-131-ortiz-vs-bonnar|title=Will Brooks vs. Michael Chandler co-headlines 'Bellator 131: Tito vs. Bonnar' |publisher=MMAjunkie.com |author=Staff|access-date=2014-09-06|date=2014-09-06}}\n\nAdditionally, it was announced that the co-main event would be a rematch between current interim lightweight champion Will Brooks and former undisputed champion Michael Chandler, for the vacant world title.\n\n[[Muhammed Lawal]] was originally scheduled to face Tom DeBlass on this card. However, on November 1, it was announced that DeBlass had suffered a cut during training and had to withdraw from the bout.{{cite news|url=http://mmajunkie.com/2014/11/nasty-cut-forces-tom-deblass-out-of-king-mo-fight-at-bellator-131|title=Nasty cut forces Tom DeBlass out of 'King Mo' fight at Bellator 131 |publisher=MMAjunkie.com |author=Staff|access-date=2014-11-01|date=2014-11-02}} Lawal instead faced [[Joe Vedepo]].\n\nThis event was the highest rated in Bellator's history, garnering an average viewership of 1.2 million television viewers in the U.S. with a peak of over 2 million viewers in the main event.{{cite news|url=http://mmajunkie.com/2014/11/spike-tv-bellator-131-tito-vs-bonnar-peaks-with-2-million-viewers|title=Spike TV: 'Bellator 131: Tito vs. Bonnar' peaks with 2 million viewers |publisher=MMAjunkie.com |author=Staff|access-date=2014-11-18|date=2014-11-18}}\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Main card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Light Heavyweight\n|[[Tito Ortiz]]\n|def.\n|[[Stephan Bonnar]]\n|Decision (split) (30-27, 28-29, 30-27)\n|3\n|5:00\n|\n}}\n|-\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Lightweight\n|[[Will Brooks]] (ic)\n|def.\n|[[Michael Chandler]]\n|TKO (punches)\n|4\n|3:48\n| For the [[List of Bellator champions#Lightweight Championship|vacant Bellator Lightweight Championship]]\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Middleweight\n|[[Joe Schilling]]\n|def.\n|[[Melvin Manhoef]]\n|KO (punch)\n|2\n|0:32\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Catchweight (143 lb)\n|[[Mike Richman]]\n|def.\n|[[Nam Phan]]\n|TKO (punches)\n|1\n|0:46\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Light Heavyweight\n|[[Muhammed Lawal]]\n|def.\n|[[Joe Vedepo]]\n|TKO (punches)\n|3\n|0:39\n|\n}}\n|-\n! colspan=\"8\" style=\"background-color: #ccf; color: #000080; text-align: center;\" | '''Preliminary Card (Spike.com)'''\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Middleweight\n|[[A.J. Matthews]]\n|def.\n|Kyle Bolt\n|TKO (punches)\n|1\n|1:39\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Flyweight\n|Jonathan Santa Maria\n|def.\n|Ron Henderson\n|Decision (split) (29-28, 28-29, 30-27)\n|3\n|5:00\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Featherweight\n|Jordan Bailey\n|def.\n|Alex Higley\n|Submission (rear-naked choke)\n|1\n|3:27\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Flyweight\n|Nick Garcia\n|def.\n|Matthew Ramirez\n|Submission (guillotine choke)\n|2\n|0:56\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Welterweight\n|[[Andy Murad]]\n|def.\n|Bubba Pugh\n|Decision (split) (29-28, 28-29, 29-28)\n|3\n|5:00\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Bantamweight\n|[[Rolando Perez]]\n|vs.\n|Mark Vorgeas\n|Split Draw (29-27, 26-30, 28-28)\n|3\n|5:00\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Lightweight\n|Joao Faria\n|def.\n|Ian Butler\n|Submission (head and arm choke)\n|3\n|1:58\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent end|note=yes}}\n\n\n==References==\n{{Reflist|30em}}\n\n==External links==\n*[http://www.bellator.com Bellator]\n\n{{Bellator Tournament Events}}\n\n[[Category:2014 American television seasons]]\n[[Category:2014 in mixed martial arts]]\n[[Category:Bellator MMA by year]]"}}}]},"44417196":{"pageid":44417196,"ns":0,"title":"2015 in Bellator MMA","revisions":[{"slots":{"main":{"contentmodel":"wikitext","contentformat":"text/x-wiki","*":"{{short description|Mixed martial arts events}}\n{{Infobox year in combat sports\n| name = 2015 in Bellator MMA\n| image = Bellator MMA Logo.svg\n| image_size = 150px\n| alt =\n| caption =\n| promotion = [[Bellator MMA]]\n| first_date = \n| first_date_aired = {{Start date|2015|01|16}}\n| last_date =\n| last_date_aired = {{End date|2015|12|04}}\n| total_events = \n| total_fights = \n| title_fights = \n| preceded_by = [[2014 in Bellator MMA|2014]]\n| followed_by = [[2016 in Bellator MMA|2016]]\n}}\n\n'''2015 in Bellator MMA''' was the seventh year in the history of [[Bellator MMA]], a [[mixed martial arts]] promotion based in the United States. Bellator held '''16 events''' in 2015.\n\n==Background==\nIn June 2014, Founder and CEO [[Bjorn Rebney]] parted with the company.{{cite web|last=Stupp|first=Dann|title=Bellator announces departure of executives Bjorn Rebney and Tim Danaher|date=18 June 2014|url=http://mmajunkie.com/2014/06/bellator-announces-departure-of-executives-bjorn-rebney-and-tim-danaher|publisher=MMA Junkie|access-date=June 18, 2014}} Former [[Strikeforce (mixed martial arts)|Strikeforce]] founder [[Scott Coker]] was announced as the new President of Bellator MMA.{{cite web|url=http://mmajunkie.com/2014/06/former-strikeforce-head-scott-coker-named-bellator-mma-president|title=Former Strikeforce head Scott Coker named Bellator MMA president|publisher=MMA Junkie|access-date=2014-06-18|date=2014-06-18}} Beginning this year, Bellator would drop its original, weekly, seasonal tournament format and adopt a traditional monthly schedule.{{cite web|url=http://www.fightersonlymag.com/content/news/21271-scott-coker-addresses-bellator-nation|title=Scott Coker Addresses 'Bellator Nation'|publisher=fightersonlymag.com|access-date=2014-06-27|date=2014-07-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140725193624/http://www.fightersonlymag.com/content/news/21271-scott-coker-addresses-bellator-nation|archive-date=2014-07-25|url-status=dead}}\n\n2015 would also see a collaboration between Bellator and kickboxing promotion [[Glory (kickboxing)|Glory]], both of which aired fight cards on [[Spike TV]]. Announced in June, [[Bellator MMA & Glory: Dynamite 1]] (or Bellator 142: Dynamite 1) was broadcast live on September 19.{{cite web|url=http://www.mmamania.com/2015/6/19/8816861/bellator-dynamite-feature-title-fight-one-night-light-heavyweight-tourney-glory-kickboxing-san-jose|title=Bellator 'Dynamite' to feature title fight, one-night light heavyweight tourney, and GLORY kickboxing in San Jose|publisher=mmamania.com|author=Michael Stets|date=2015-06-19|access-date=2015-08-06}}\n\n==Bellator 132==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator 132: Pitbull vs. Straus 2\n|image=\n|date= January 16, 2015\n|venue= [[Pechanga Resort & Casino]]\n|purse=$243,200\n|city= [[Temecula, California]]\n|attendance= 1,300\n}}\n\n'''Bellator 132: Pitbull vs. Straus 2''' took place January 16, 2015 at Pechanga Resort & Casino in Temecula, California. The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nA [[Bellator Featherweight World Championship]] rematch between [[Patr\u00edcio Pitbull]] and [[Daniel Straus (fighter)|Daniel Straus]] headlined the event. The event aired live during prime time on Spike TV, and was followed up with an encore of the entire event.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe main card of Bellator 134 was announced on the air during [[Bellator 131]]. President Scott Coker announced the main card fights would feature fighters representing the United States taking on fighters representing the United Kingdom.\n\nThe event was headlined by a Light Heavyweight Championship match between current champion Emanuel Newton and [[Bellator MMA: 2014 Summer Series#Light Heavyweight tournament bracket|Bellator 2014 Summer Series Light Heavyweight Tournament Winner]] Liam McGeary.\n\n[[Douglas Lima]] was originally scheduled to defend his Welterweight title against [[Paul Daley]] on this card. However, in early January 2015, he pulled out of the bout due to an injury.{{cite web|url=http://www.mmafighting.com/2015/1/20/7858865/devastated-douglas-lima-injured-out-of-bellator-134-title-defense|title='Devastated' Douglas Lima injured, out of Bellator 134 title defense against Paul Daley|publisher=mmafighting.com|author=Shaun Al-Shatti|date=2015-01-20|access-date=2015-02-24}}\n\n[[Michael Page (fighter)|Michael Page]] was expected to face [[Curtis Millender]] but withdrew due to a cut over his left eye and was replaced by [[Brennan Ward]].{{cite web|url=http://www.mmafighting.com/2015/2/23/8091985/michael-page-out-of-bellator-134-brennan-ward-fills-in-to-face-curtis|title=Michael Page out of Bellator 134, Brennan Ward fills in to face Curtis Millender|publisher=mmafighting.com|author=Marc Raimondi|date=2015-02-23|access-date=2015-02-24}} As a result of the move, Ward's original opponent, [[Jesse Juarez]], was pulled from the card altogether.\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Main Card (Spike TV)}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n| Light Heavyweight\n| [[Liam McGeary]]\n| def.\n| [[Emanuel Newton]] (c)\n| Decision (unanimous) (48-46, 48-47, 48-47)\n| 5\n| 5:00\n| For the [[List of Bellator champions#Light Heavyweight World Championship|Bellator Light Heavyweight Championship]]\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Heavyweight\n|[[Muhammed Lawal]]\n|def.\n|[[Cheick Kongo]]\n|Decision (split) (30-27, 28-29, 29-28)\n|3\n|5:00\n|}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Welterweight\n| [[Paul Daley]]\n|def.\n| [[Andr\u00e9 Santos (fighter)|Andr\u00e9 Santos]]\n|Decision (unanimous) (29-27, 29-28, 29-28)\n|3\n|5:00\n|}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Light Heavyweight\n|[[Linton Vassell]]\n|def.\n|[[Rameau Thierry Sokoudjou]]\n|TKO (punches)\n|2\n|3:18\n|}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Welterweight\n|[[Brennan Ward]]\n|def.\n|[[Curtis Millender]]\n|Submission (rear-naked choke)\n|1\n|1:39\n|}}\n|-\n! The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThis event headlined the Bellator Bantamweight Championship between champion Joe Warren and challenger Marcos Galvao.\n\n[[Mike Richman]] was expected to face [[Eduardo Dantas]] but forced out by injury. As a result, L.C. Davis vs. Hideo Tokoro elevated to the co-main event.\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Main Card (Spike TV)}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n| Bantamweight\n| [[Marcos Galv\u00e3o]]\n| def.\n| [[Joe Warren (fighter)|Joe Warren]] (c)\n| Verbal Submission (kneebar)\n| 2\n| 0:45\n| For the [[List of Bellator champions#Bantamweight World Championship|Bellator Bantamweight Championship]]\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n| Bantamweight\n| [[L.C. The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThis event was headlined by Lightweight Championship match between current champion [[Will Brooks]] and Season 7 Lightweight Tournament Winner [[Dave Jansen]].\n\nThe co-main event was a middleweight fight between longtime kickboxer [[Joe Schilling]] and [[Rafael Carvalho]].\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Main Card (Spike TV)}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n| Lightweight\n| [[Will Brooks]] (c)\n| def.\n| [[Dave Jansen]]\n| Decision (unanimous) (49-46, 49-46, 49-46)\n| 5\n| 5:00\n| For the [[List of Bellator champions#Lightweight World Championship|Bellator Lightweight Championship]]\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n| Middleweight\n| [[Rafael Carvalho]]\n| def.\n| [[Joe Schilling]]\n| Decision (split) (29-28, 28-29, 30-27)\n| 3\n| 5:00\n|}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n| Lightweight\n| [[Marcin Held]]\n| def.\n| [[Alexander Sarnavskiy]]\n| Verbal Submission (kneebar)\n| 3\n| 1:11\n|}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n| Heavyweight\n| [[Tony Johnson (fighter)|Tony Johnson]]\n| def.\n| [[Alexander Volkov (fighter)|Alexander Volkov]]\n| Decision (split) (29-28, 29-28, 28-29)\n| 3\n| 5:00\n|}}\n|-\n! McKee]]\n|def.\n|Marcos Bonilla\n|Submission (rear-naked choke)\n|1\n|2:08\n|}}\n{{MMAevent end|note=yes}}\n{{Cite web|url = http://www.bellator.com/fight-card/bellator-136|title = Bellator 136 Fight Card|date = 2015-04-10|access-date = 2015-04-10|website = bellator.com }}\n\n==Bellator 137==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator 137: Halsey vs. Grove\n|image=\n|date= May 15, 2015\n|venue= [[Pechanga Resort and Casino]]\n|purse=$310,040\n|city= [[Temecula, California]]\n|attendance= 1,200\n}}\n\n'''Bellator 137: Halsey vs. Grove''' took place May 15, 2015 at the Pechanga Resort and Casino in Temecula, California. The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event was expected to be headlined by a [[Bellator Middleweight Championship]] bout between then champion [[Brandon Halsey]] and [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] veteran [[Kendall Grove]]. However, Halsey came in overweight at the weigh-ins, weighing in at 188.1 lb. This prompted Bellator to create a stipulation that if Halsey won the bout, the championship would be vacated. If Grove won the bout, he would become the undisputed champion.\n\nThe co-main event featured a [[List of Bellator champions#Bantamweight World Championship|Bellator Bantamweight Championship]] title eliminator bout between former champion [[Eduardo Dantas]] and [[Mike Richman]]. This bout was briefly in jeopardy as Richman missed weight and Dantas agreed for the fight to continue under the condition that Richman wouldn't weight more than 147 pounds on fight night, but Richman declined. However, both fighters' camps agreed to new stipulations the day of the fight.{{cite web|url=http://www.mmafighting.com/2015/5/14/8609643/eduardo-dantas-vs-mike-richman-scrapped-from-bellator-137|title=Eduardo Dantas vs. Mike Richman scrapped from Bellator 137 (updated)|publisher=mmafighting.com|author=Guilherme Cruz|access-date=2015-05-15|date=2015-05-15}}\n\n[[A.J. Matthews]] was expected to face Ben Reiter at the event. However, Matthews was forced out of the bout and was replaced by [[Strikeforce (mixed martial arts)|Strikeforce]] and UFC veteran [[Benji Radach]].\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Main Card (Spike TV)}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n| Catchweight (189 lb)\n| [[Brandon Halsey]]\n| def.\n| [[Kendall Grove]]\n| TKO (punches)\n| 4\n| 2:25\n| For the [[List of Bellator MMA champions#Middleweight World Championship|Bellator Middleweight World Championship]]. Halsey missed weight and was immediately stripped of the championship. Title was at stake for Grove only.\n|}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n| Catchweight (140 lb)\n| [[Eduardo Dantas]]\n| def.\n| [[Mike Richman]]\n| Decision (unanimous) (29-28, 29-28, 29-28)\n| 3\n| 5:00\n| [[List of Bellator champions#Bantamweight World Championship|Bellator Bantamweight Championship]] title eliminator.\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n| Welterweight\n| [[Fernando Gonzalez (fighter)|Fernando Gonzalez]]\n| def.\n| [[Curtis Millender]]\n| Submission (guillotine choke)\n| 3\n| 1:14\n|}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n| Bantamweight\n| [[Darrion Caldwell]]\n| def.\n| [[Rafael Silva (fighter)|Rafael Silva]]\n| Decision (unanimous) (29-28, 29-28, 29-28)\n| 3\n| 5:00\n|}}\n|-\n! The two were originally expected to fight on October 4, 2008 at the [[BankAtlantic Center]] in [[Sunrise, Florida]] as part of [[CBS]]' ''Saturday Night Fights'' at [[EliteXC: Heat]]. However, Shamrock received a cut to the left eye during a warm-up only hours before the fight was to take place. That bout was eventually rescheduled for this event.\n\nThe co-main event was originally expected to feature a [[List of Bellator champions#Featherweight World Championship|Bellator Featherweight Championship]] bout between current champion [[Patr\u00edcio Freire]] and former [[WSOF Featherweight Championship|WSOF Featherweight champion]] [[Georgi Karakhanyan]]. However, Karakhanyan was forced out of the bout due to an injury and was replaced by Season 10 Featherweight Tournament winner [[Daniel Weichel]].\t\n\n[[Bobby Lashley]] was originally scheduled to face [[James Thompson (fighter)|James Thompson]] at this event.{{cite web|url=http://mmajunkie.com/2015/04/bobby-lashley-vs-james-thompson-rematch-set-for-bellator-138-in-st-louis|title=Bobby Lashley vs. James Thompson rematch set for Bellator 138 in St. Louis|publisher=mmajunkie.com|author=Brent Brookhouse|date=April 13, 2015}} However, on June 10, it was announced that Thompson pulled out of the bout due to injury and was replaced by [[Dan Charles (fighter)|Dan Charles]].{{cite web|url=http://mmajunkie.com/2015/06/james-thompson-injured-dan-charles-steps-in-vs-bobby-lashley-at-bellator-138|title=James Thompson injured, Dan Charles steps in vs. Bobby Lashley at Bellator 138|publisher=mmajunkie.com|author=Mike Bohn|date=10 June 2015}}\n\nBellator 138 was the highest rated Bellator event to date before Bellator 149. It did an average of 1.6 million viewers for the whole event and a peak of 2.4 million during the Kimbo Slice and Ken Shamrock fight with a DVR peak of 2.9 million. The previous high was Bellator 131 which did 1.2 million average for the entire event and a peak of 2 million during the Tito Ortiz and Stephan Bonnar fight and a DVR peak of 2.2 million.\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Main Card (Spike TV)}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Catchweight (232 lb)\n| [[Kimbo Slice]]\n|def.\n| [[Ken Shamrock]]\n|KO (punches)\n|1\n|2:22\n|\n}}\n|-\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Featherweight\n|[[Patr\u00edcio Freire]] (c)\n|def.\n|[[Daniel Weichel]]\n|KO (punch)\n|2\n|0:32\n|For the [[List of Bellator champions#Featherweight World Championship|Bellator Featherweight Championship]].\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Heavyweight\n| [[Bobby Lashley]]\n|def.\n| [[Dan Charles (fighter)|Dan Charles]]\n|TKO (punches)\n|2\n|4:14\n|}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Featherweight\n| [[Daniel Mason-Straus]]\n|def.\n| [[Henry Corrales]]\n|Submission (guillotine choke)\n|2\n|3:47\n|}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Lightweight\n| [[Michael Chandler]]\n|def.\n| [[Derek Campos]]\n|Submission (rear-naked choke)\n|1\n|2:17\n|}}\n|-\n! Siscoe\n| Submission (rear-naked choke)\n| 2\n| 1:26\n|}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n| Middleweight\n| Enrique Watson\n| def.\n| Kain Royer\n| Submission (rear-naked choke)\n| 1\n| 0:41\n|}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n| Catchweight (165 lb)\n| Rashard Lovelace\n| def.\n| Matt Helm\n| TKO (leg kick)\n| 1\n| 0:58\n|}}\n{{MMAevent end|note=yes}}\n{{Cite web|url = http://www.bellator.com/fight-card/bellator-138|title = Bellator 138 Fight Card|date = 2015-06-20|website = bellator.com }}\n\n==Bellator 139==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator 139: Kongo vs. Volkov\n|image=\n|date= June 26, 2015\n|venue= [[Kansas Star Casino]]\n|city= [[Mulvane, Kansas]]\n|attendance= 2,500\n}}\n\n'''Bellator 139: Kongo vs. Volkov''' took place June 26, 2015 at Kansas Star Casino in Mulvane, Kansas. The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe main event was a Welterweight fight between [[Paul Daley]] and Andy Uhrich.\n\nThe event was expected to be headlined by a [[welterweight]] bout between [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] veteran [[Josh Koscheck]] and Matt Secor. However Koscheck pulled out of the bout due to an injury. As a result, [[Paul Daley]] vs. Andy Uhrich was elevated to the main event\n\nAlso on the card [[Paul Bradley (fighter)|Paul Bradley]] faces [[Chris Honeycutt]] in a rematch. Secor|date=2016-01-29|website=bellator.com}}{{Dead link|date=July 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}\n\n==Bellator 149==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator 149: Shamrock vs. Gracie III\n|image=\n|image_size=320px\n|date=February 19, 2016\n|venue=[[Toyota Center]]\n|city=[[Houston, Texas]]\n|attendance= 14,209\n|gate=$1,388,951\n}}\n'''Bellator 149: Shamrock vs. Gracie III''' took place February 19, 2016, at the Toyota Center in Houston, Texas. The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV, drawing an average 2.0 million viewers.[http://mmapayout.com/2016/02/bellator-149-draw-1-9m-kimbo-dada-draw-2-5m-viewers/ Bellator 149 draw 1.9M, Kimbo-Dada draw 2.5M viewers] - MMA Payout, 22 February 2016\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe main event and co-main event of Bellator 149 were announced on the air during Bellator 145. President [[Scott Coker]] announced the main event fight would feature trilogy bout between [[combat sport]]s legends [[Ken Shamrock]] and [[Royce Gracie]]. Gracie initially beat Shamrock in fifty-seven seconds via rear-naked choke at their first meeting at [[UFC 1]] in 1993. Subsequent to that bout, the duo fought to a thirty-six minute draw at [[UFC 5]] in 1995.\n\nThe co-main event featured a heavyweight bout between former [[Miami-Dade County, Florida|Miami-Dade County]] [[Street fighting|street fighters]] Kevin Ferguson, aka \"[[Kimbo Slice]]\" and Dhafir Harris, aka \"Dada 5000\"\n\nDuring intermission after the [[Kimbo Slice]] vs. [[Dada 5000]] fight and shortly before the [[Ken Shamrock]] vs. [[Royce Gracie]] bout, [[Bellator MMA]] ring announcer Michael C. Williams announced to the live [[Toyota Center]] crowd that the attendance was 14,209. Thus making Bellator 149 the largest attended show in [[Bellator MMA]] history, beating out [[Bellator MMA & Glory: Dynamite 1]] previous live attendance of 11,732.\n\nFollowing the event it was announced that both [[Ken Shamrock]] and [[Kimbo Slice]] had failed their pre-fight drug tests. Shamrock tested positive for the anabolic steroid [[nandrolone]], the opioid [[methadone]], and an elevated (T/E) ratio of 12.4:1. Meanwhile, Slice also tested positive for nandrolone and having an elevated (T/E) ratio of 6.4:1. The maximum allowed (T/E) ratio by both the [[Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation]] and the [[World Anti-Doping Agency]] is 4:1.{{cite web|last=Raimondi |first= Marc |url=http://www.mmafighting.com/2016/3/21/11279344/kimbo-slice-ken-shamrock-both-test-positive-for-steroids-at-bellator |title=Kimbo Slice, Ken Shamrock both test positive for steroids at Bellator 149 |publisher=MMAfighting.com |date=March 21, 2016 |access-date=March 21, 2016}} On May 2, 2016, it was revealed that Slice had settled with the Texas Athletic Commission with a fine of $2,500 and a revoking of his license in the state of Texas. The result of the bout has also been changed to a [[no contest (combat sports)|no contest]].{{cite web|last=Marrocco |first= Steven |url=http://mmajunkie.com/2016/05/bellators-kimbo-slice-settles-with-texas-commission-following-failed-steroid-test |title=Bellator's 'Kimbo Slice' settles with Texas commission following failed steroid test |publisher=MMAjunkie.com |date=May 2, 2016 |access-date=May 2, 2016}}\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Light Heavyweight \n|[[Royce 3,288\n|gate=$215,185\n}}\n'''Bellator 150: Kongo vs. Spartan''' took place February 26, 2016, at the Kansas Star Casino in Mulvane, Kansas. The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event was expected to be headlined by a rematch between [[Marcos Galv\u00e3o]] and [[Eduardo Dantas]] for the [[List of Bellator champions#Bantamweight World Championship|Bellator Bantamweight Championship]]. The bantamweight title rematch was originally scheduled for Bellator 144, but was postponed when Dantas was forced to withdraw after suffering a rib injury in training. Dantas defeated Galv\u00e3o via second-round knockout in their first meeting at Bellator 89 when \u201cDudu\u201d was the promotion's reigning 135-pound champ. However, due to an illness throughout the week leading to the fight, Galv\u00e3o was pulled from the card the day of the weigh ins.{{cite web|url=http://mmajunkie.com/2016/02/on-eve-of-bellator-150-marcos-galvao-vs-eduardo-dantas-title-fight-pulled-from-card|title=On eve of Bellator 150, Marcos Galvao vs. Eduardo Dantas title fight pulled from card |date=2016-02-25 |website=MMAjunkie.com |publisher=MMA Junkie Staff}}\n\nThe co-main event featured local favorite [[David Rickels]] facing off against Bobby 151==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator 151: Warren vs. Caldwell\n|image=\n|image_size=320px\n|date=March 4, 2016\n|venue=[[WinStar World Casino]]\n|city=[[Thackerville, Oklahoma]]\n|attendance= 1,152\n|gate= $103,710\n}}\n'''Bellator 151: Warren vs. Caldwell''' took place March 4, 2016, at the [[WinStar World Casino]] in [[Thackerville, Oklahoma]]. The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event was headlined by a Bantamweight bout between [[Joe Warren (fighter)|Joe Warren]] and undefeated rising star [[Darrion Caldwell]]. A former two-division champion, Warren has won six of his last seven fights in [[Bellator MMA]]. The 39-year-old last appeared at Bellator 143 on Sept. 25, when he captured a unanimous verdict against [[L.C. Davis]]. The 27-year-old Caldwell is 8\u20130 in his burgeoning career, including five triumphs under the Bellator banner. In his last outing, the former NCAA national champion wrestler choked out [[Shawn Bunch]] inside of a round at Bellator 143.\n\n[[Michael Page (fighter)|Michael Page]] was originally scheduled to face [[Fernando Gonzalez (fighter)|Fernando Gonzalez]] at this event but was pulled out of the bout in early February 2016. He was replaced by [[Resurrection Fighting Alliance]] welterweight champion Gilbert Smith.{{cite web|url=http://mmajunkie.com/2016/02/michael-page-out-of-bellator-151-rfa-champ-gilbert-smith-in-vs-fernando-gonzalez|title=Michael Page out of Bellator 151, RFA champ Gilbert Smith in vs. Fernando 153==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator 153: Koreshkov vs. Henderson\n|image=\n|image_size=320px\n|date=April 22, 2016\n|venue=[[Mohegan Sun Arena]]\n|city=[[Uncasville, Connecticut]]\n|attendance= 9,043\n|gate= $687,269\n}}\n\n'''Bellator 153: Koreshkov vs. Henderson''' took place April 22, 2016, at the [[Mohegan Sun Arena]] in [[Uncasville, Connecticut]]. The event aired live in prime time on [[Spike TV]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event was headlined by a Welterweight Championship match between current champion [[Andrey Koreshkov]] and former [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] and [[World Extreme Cagefighting|WEC]] lightweight champion [[Benson Henderson]]. The 32-year-old Henderson recently ended a 14-fight run with the [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] by signing a multi-fight deal with [[Bellator MMA]]. A longtime 155-pounder, Henderson recorded back-to-back wins as a welterweight in 2015. Also on the card is the [[Bellator MMA|Bellator]] debut of [[Evangelista Santos]] taking on long time contender [[Brennan Ward]].\n\nFormer Bellator Featherweight Champion [[Patr\u00edcio Pitbull]] was originally scheduled to face [[John Macap\u00e1]]. who had to pull out of the evening's co-feature bout with a broken rib.\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight 154==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator 154: Davis vs. King Mo\n|image=\n|image_size=320px\n|date=May 14, 2016\n|venue=[[SAP Center]]\n|city=[[San Jose, California]]\n|attendance= 11,084\n|gate= $984,552\n}}\n\n'''''Bellator 154: Davis vs. King Mo''''' is a [[mixed martial arts]] event held on May 14, 2016, at the [[SAP Center]] in [[San Jose, California, USA]]. The event was aired live in prime time on [[Spike TV]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nDavis vs. King Mo was announced during Bellator 149 in Houston. The two men were supposed to face each other in the finals of the [[Bellator MMA & Glory: Dynamite 1]] light heavyweight one-night tournament back in September, but \"King Mo\" sustained a hip injury after winning in the first round. Former [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] star [[Phil Davis (fighter)|Phil Davis]] won the tournament at Dynamite by submitting [[Emanuel Newton]] and knocked out reserve fighter [[Francis Carmont]]. Davis was originally scheduled to challenge light heavyweight champion [[Liam McGeary]], but McGeary was injured. Lawal won the two-night, eight-man tournament at [[Rizin Fighting Federation]] on New Year's Eve in Japan. He knocked out [[Brett McDermott]] in the first round, beat Teodoras Aukstuolis in the semifinals by unanimous decision and knocked out Jiri Prochazka in the final. The winner of the main event will challenge for the title against the current champion.\n\nFormer Bellator Lightweight Champion [[Michael Chandler]] was scheduled to face former Strikeforce Lightweight Champion [[Josh Thomson]] in a lightweight bout. However, on May 2, it was announced that Thomson pulled out of the bout due to an undisclosed injury. As a result, Chandler was pulled from the card altogether.\n\n[[Jordan Parsons]] was scheduled to face Adam Piccolotti in a featherweight bout on this card. That fight was cancelled after Parsons was involved in a hit-and-run accident that left him hospitalized before he died on May 4, 2016.\n\n[[Sergei Kharitonov]] was scheduled to make his debut on this card against Josh Appelt. However, on May 11, Kharitonov withdrew from the bout due to illness. As a result, Appelt was also removed from the card.\n\n[[Darren Uyenoyama]] was scheduled to fight on this card against Alvin Cacdac but required medical testing revealed a condition that would not allow Darren to compete.\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Light Heavyweight \n|[[Phil Davis (fighter)|Phil Davis]]\n|def.\n|[[Muhammed event \n|name=Bellator 155: [[Carvalho]] vs. [[Manhoef]]\n|image=\n|image_size=320px\n|date=May 20, 2016\n|venue=[[CenturyLink Arena]]\n|city=[[Boise, Idaho]]\n|attendance= 6,120\n|gate= $497,778\n}}\n'''Bellator 155: Carvalho vs Manhoef''' took place May 20, 2016, at the CenturyLink Arena in Boise, Idaho. The event aired live in prime time on [[Spike TV]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event was headlined by a match between [[Rafael Carvalho]] and [[Melvin Manhoef]] for the [[List of Bellator champions#Middleweight World Championship|Bellator Middleweight Championship]]. Carvalho pulled off one of 2015's biggest upsets when he finished [[Brandon Halsey]] with a body kick in the second round to claim the Middleweight title at Bellator 144 last October. The Brazilian has not lost since his MMA debut in 2011 and has stopped 10 of his last 12 opponents. Manhoef earned his shot at the title by knocking out [[Hisaki Kato]] in the opening round at Bellator 146.\n\nThe co-main event featured former [[List of Bellator champions#Featherweight World Championship|Bellator Featherweight Championship]] Champion [[Pat Curran (fighter)|Pat Curran]] facing off against former [[World Series of Fighting]] [[World Series of Fighting#Featherweight Championship|featherweight champion]] [[Georgi Karakhanyan]].\n\nThis event was scheduled to crown the inaugural Bellator women's featherweight champion in a bout between Marloes Coenen and [[Julia Budd]]. However, Budd was injured and replaced by Alexis Dufresne thus changing the fight to a non-title bout.\n\nA preliminary bout between Ricky Steele and Eric Cronkhite was cancelled after Cronkhite missed weight by 9 pounds.\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Middleweight\n|[[Rafael Carvalho]] (c)\n|def.\n|[[Melvin Manhoef]]\n|Decision (split) 156==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator 156: Galvao vs. Dantas 2\n|image=\n|image_size=320px\n|date=June 17, 2016\n|venue=[[Save Mart Center]]\n|attendance= 5,552\n|gate= $451,578\n|city=[[Fresno, California]]\n}}\n'''Bellator 156: Galvao vs. Dantas 2''' took place on June 17, 2016, at the [[Save Mart Center]] in [[Fresno, California]]. The event aired live in prime time on [[Spike TV]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\n[[Marcos Galv\u00e3o]] made the first defense of his [[List of Bellator champions#Bantamweight World Championship|Bellator Bantamweight Championship]] title against [[Eduardo Dantas]]. The rematch was originally scheduled for Bellator 150, but was scrapped following a last-minute illness suffered by Galv\u00e3o. Both fighters cut their teeth with [[Andr\u00e9 Pederneiras]]\u2019 [[Nova Uni\u00e3o (mixed martial arts)|Nova Uni\u00e3o]] squad in [[Rio de Janeiro]], until their paths crossed at Bellator 89. Dantas won the fight via a second-round knockout. Dantas went on to defend the title against [[Anthony Leone (fighter)|Anthony Leone]] before losing it to [[Joe Warren (fighter)|Joe Warren]] at Bellator 128. In turn, Galv\u00e3o pieced together three consecutive victories and then defeated Warren via second-round technical submission to become the new champion.\n\n[[Douglas Lima]] was originally scheduled to face [[Chidi Njokuani]], but was pulled from this bout when he got the call to headline Bellator 158 in London against [[Paul Daley]] due to an injury that forced [[Josh Koscheck]] out of that match up. \n \n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Bantamweight\n|[[Eduardo Dantas]]\n|def.\n|[[Marcos Galv\u00e3o]] (c)\n|Decision (unanimous) (50-45, 50-44, 50-43)\n|5\n|5:00\n| For the [[List of Bellator champions#Bantamweight World Championship|Bellator Bantamweight Championship]].\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Welterweight\n|[[Chidi Njokuani]]\n|def.\n|Thiago Jambo\n|KO (body kick and punches)\n|3\n|2:39\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Middleweight\n|[[John Salter]]\n|def.\n|[[Brandon Halsey]]\n|Submission (triangle choke)\n|1\n|4:03\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Middleweight\n|[[Chris Honeycutt]]\n|def.\n|[[Mikkel Parlo]]\n|Decision (unanimous) (29-28, 30-27, 30-27)\n|3\n|5:00\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent card|Preliminary card (Spike.com)|header=no}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Middleweight\n|[[Ben Reiter]]\n|def.\n|[[A.J. Jackson had a successful three-fight stint with [[Bellator MMA]] - two knockouts against [[Joey Beltran]] and [[Christian M'Pumbu]] plus a unanimous decision won over [[Muhammed Lawal]] - before returning to the UFC where he defeated [[Fabio Maldonado]] via unanimous decision at [[UFC 186]]. After facing Maldonado, a contract settlement brought Jackson back to Bellator MMA. A 2008 Olympic gold medalist in judo, Ishii began his MMA career in December 2009 and has competed against fighters such as [[Fedor Emelianenko]], [[Mirko Cro Cop]], [[Jerome Le Banner]], and [[Tim Sylvia]].\n\nIn the co-main event, former [[Bellator MMA|Bellator]] Lightweight Champion [[Michael Chandler]] took on top contender [[Patricky Freire]] for the vacant Bellator Lightweight Championship.\n\nLike the previous ''Dynamite'' card, the show combined MMA and kickboxing bouts with a cage and ring set up side-by-side. ''Bellator Kickboxing: St. Louis'' - which featured a rematch between Joe Schilling and Hisaki Kato under kickboxing rules - aired immediately following the ''Dynamite 2'' portion on Spike TV.\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Catchweight (225 lb)\n|[[Rampage Jackson|Quinton Jackson]]\n|def.\n|[[Satoshi Ishii]]\n|Decision (split) (29-28, (GBP)\n$1,155,181 (USD)\n|city=[[London, England]]\n}}\n'''Bellator 158: Daley vs. Lima''' (aka ''Bellator: London'') was held on July 16, 2016, at the [[O2 Arena (London)]] in [[London]]. The event had a tape-delayed broadcast on [[Spike TV]] and [[Channel 5 (UK)]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nOriginally, Bellator President [[Scott Coker]] announced that [[Kimbo Slice]] and [[James Thompson (fighter)|James Thompson]] would compete in the main event of Bellator 158, to take place July 16 at London's [[O2 Arena (London)|O2 Arena]].{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mma/story/_/id/15225373/kimbo-slice-james-thompson-co-headline-bellator-event-london-july-16|title=Kimbo Slice-James Thompson II booked for July 16 in London|work=ESPN|date=April 18, 2016|access-date=June 7, 2016|author=Okamoto, Brett}} This was to be a rematch of their infamous 2008 clash under the [[EliteXC]] banner which ended in a controversial TKO win for Kimbo. Tragically these plans had to be scrapped, as Slice died suddenly on June 6, 2016, of heart failure.{{cite web|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/more-sports/mma-fighter-kimbo-slice-hospital-report-article-1.2663701|title=Mixed martial arts fighter Kimbo Slice dies at 42|date=2016-06-07|website=nydailynews.com|publisher=New York Daily News|last=Christopher|first=Brennan}}\n\n[[Josh Koscheck]] was scheduled to make his debut on this card against [[Paul Daley]]. However, Koscheck withdrew from the bout and was replaced by [[Douglas Lima]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sherdog.com/news/news/Josh-Koscheck-Out-of-Bellator-158-Paul-Daley-to-Meet-ExChamp-Douglas-Lima-in-London-106065#!|title=JOSH KOSCHECK OUT OF BELLATOR 158; PAUL DALEY TO MEET EX-CHAMP DOUGLAS LIMA IN LONDON|date=2016-06-06|website=sherdog.com|publisher=Sherdog}}\n\n[[Fernando Gonzalez (fighter)|Fernando Gonzalez]] was supposed to fight [[Michael Page (fighter)|Michael Page]] but visa issues forced him off the card and was replaced by [[Evangelista Santos]].{{cite web|url=http://mmajunkie.com/2016/06/with-card-official-michael-page-now-meets-evangelista-santos-at-bellator-158-in-london|title=With card official, Michael Page now meets Evangelista Santos at Bellator 158 in London|date=2016-06-09|website=MMAjunkie.com|publisher=MMA Junkie Staff}}\n\nContractual issues with ATAK Promotions caused Mark Godbeer and Ben Smith to withdraw from the $206,978\n|city=[[Mulvane, Kansas]]\n}}\n\n'''Bellator 159: Caldwell vs. Taimanglo''' was held on July 22, 2016, at the Kansas Star Arena in [[Mulvane, Kansas]]. The event aired live in prime time on [[Spike TV]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event was headlined by a bantamweight title eliminator bout between [[Darrion Caldwell]] and [[Joe Taimanglo]]. The winner is expect to face the current bantamweight champion [[Eduardo Dantas]]. Originally set at bantamweight, the fight was switched to a catchweight when Taimanglo weighed in at 138 pounds.\n\nIn the co-main event, local fighter Dave Rickels met Melvin Guillard. It was originally scheduled to be a lightweight bout, but Guillard missed weight and came in at 157.9 pounds.\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent 160==\n{{Infobox MMA event \n|name=Bellator 160: Henderson vs. Pitbull\n|image=\n|image_size=320px\n|date=August 26, 2016\n|venue= [[Honda Center]]\n|attendance= 9,139 \n|gate= $897,468\n|city=[[Anaheim, California]]\n}}\n\n'''Bellator 160: Henderson vs. Pitbull ''' was held on August 26, 2016, at the [[Honda Center]] in [[Anaheim, California]]. The event aired live in prime time on [[Spike TV]].\n\n'''Background '''\n\nThe event was headlined by a Lightweight title eliminator fight between former [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] champion [[Benson Henderson]] and former [[Bellator MMA|Bellator]] featherweight champion [[Patr\u00edcio Pitbull]]. Henderson, after being defeated in his April debut against welterweight champion [[Andrey Koreshkov]], returned to the division where he twice defeated [[Frankie Edgar]]. He has also beaten former UFC title challengers [[Nate Diaz]] and [[Donald Cerrone]]. Pitbull sought to parlay the victory to a title shot against lightweight champion [[Michael Chandler]], who claimed the belt by knocking out Pitbull's brother, Patricky, on June 24.\n\nDue to pressure from fans the feature prelim was moved back to being the co-main even on the card featuring NCAA Division I National Champion in Wrestling [[Bubba Jenkins]] versus [[Georgi Karakhanyan]]. The last time these two met Karakhanyan defeated Jenkins by guillotine choke in the first round.\n\nAdditionally, four-time NCAA Division II Champion wrestler [[Joey Davis]] made his professional MMA debut on this card; as an amateur he had a record of 5\u20130. Davis recently graduated from [[Notre Dame College]], where he accumulated an undefeated 131\u20130 record over the course of four seasons during his collegiate wrestling career. He is the only Division II wrestler in NCAA history to win four consecutive national titles, and is one of three wrestlers ever to complete a four-year college career with an undefeated record.\n\nKevin Ferguson Jr., the eldest son of [[Kimbo Slice]], was scheduled to make his Bellator debut on this card against Jonathan Tomasian. However, the bout was cancelled on August 21 due to an injury received by Ferguson.\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Lightweight\n|[[Benson Henderson]]\n|def.\n|[[Patr\u00edcio Pitbull]]\n|TKO (leg injury)\n|2\n|2:26\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Lightweight\n|[[Derek Anderson (fighter)|Derek Anderson]]\n|def.\n|[[Saad Awad]]\n|Decision (unanimous) (30-27, 29-28, 29-28)\n|3\n|5:00\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Catchweight (149 lb)\n|[[Georgi Karakhanyan]]\n| def.\n|[[Bubba Jenkins]]\n|KO (punch)\n|1\n|0:53\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Featherweight\n|[[A. The event aired live in prime time on [[Spike TV]].\n\n'''Background '''\n\nThe event was headlined by a heavyweight fight between former [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] veteran [[Cheick Kongo]] and [[Tony Johnson (fighter)|Tony Johnson]]. Kongo was currently riding a two-fight winning streak over [[Vinicius Queiroz]] and [[Alexander Volkov (fighter)|Alexander Volkov]]. Kongo also owns wins against [[Shawn Jordan]], [[Matt Mitrione]], [[Pat Barry (fighter)|Pat Barry]] and [[Mirko Filipovic]]. The bout was Kongo's third consecutive Bellator headliner slot. Meanwhile, Johnson boasted a three-fight winning streak, including a pair of victories under the Bellator banner \u2013 a January win over [[Raphael Butler]] and an April 2015 win over Volkov. Johnson also owns wins against [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] contender [[Derrick Lewis]] and former [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] champion [[Tim The event aired live in prime time on [[Spike TV]].\n\n'''Background '''\n\nBellator 162 was headlined by the return of former middleweight champion [[Alexander Shlemenko]] for the first time in approximately 18 months, as he takes on ''[[The Ultimate Fighter 3]]'' winner [[Kendall Grove]]. Shlemenko hadn't fought for [[Bellator MMA|Bellator]] since he knocked out [[Melvin Manhoef]] at Bellator 133 in February 2015. The former middleweight champ was suspended for three years by the [[California]] State Athletic Commission after failing a post-fight drug test for [[steroids]]. Shlemenko's suspension was reduced to one year, making him eligible to compete in February of this year. Shlemenko has fought twice in 2016 under the M-1 Challenge banner, scoring consecutive triumphs over [[Vyacheslav Vasilevsky]]. Grove has been victorious in three of his last four Bellator appearances, including back-to-back stoppages of Francisco France and [[Joey Beltran]].\n\nIn the co-main event [[Bobby Lashley]] squared off with [[Josh Appelt]]. Lashley entered the cage on a seven-fight winning streak, while Appelt returned to Bellator on the strength of back-to-back victories.\n\nKevin Ferguson Jr., the eldest son of the late [[Kimbo Slice]], was scheduled to make his Bellator debut on this card against Rick Bing. However, the bout was cancelled due to Bing missing weight for the fight.\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Middleweight\n|[[Alexander Shlemenko]]\n| def.\n|[[Kendall Grove]]\n|TKO (punches)\n|2\n|1:43\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Heavyweight\n|[[Bobby Lashley]]\n|def.\n|[[Josh Appelt]]\n|Submission (rear-naked choke)\n|2\n|1:43\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Lightweight\n|[[Goiti Yamauchi]]\n|def.\n|[[Ryan Couture]]\n|Submission (armbar)\n|1\n|1:01\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Middleweight\n|[[Hisaki Kato]]\n| def.\n|[[A.J. 163==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator 163: McGeary vs. Davis\n|image=\n|image_size=320px\n|date=November 4, 2016\n|venue=[[Mohegan Sun Arena]]\n|city=[[Uncasville, Connecticut]]\n|attendance= 9,156\n|gate= $755,996\n}}\n\n'''Bellator 163: McGeary vs. Davis''' was held on November 4, 2016, at the [[Mohegan Sun Arena]] in [[Uncasville, Connecticut]]. The event aired live in prime time on [[Spike TV]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nIn the main event, [[Liam McGeary]] put up his light heavyweight title in a long-awaited match up with top contender [[Phil Davis (fighter)|Phil Davis]]. This was McGeary's second title defense. McGeary won the title by defeating [[Emanuel Newton]] in a five-round unanimous decision at Bellator 134. He then defended the title against [[Tito Ortiz]] at Bellator 142. McGeary has been out of action for over a year due to a medial collateral ligament injury. Davis defeated former light heavy champion Emanuel Newton and [[Francis Carmont]] in a one-night tournament to earn the title shot. While waiting for McGeary to heal, Davis also defeated [[Muhammed Lawal]] at Bellator 154.\n\nThe scheduled co-main event of [[Marloes Coenen]] vs. [[Talita Nogueira]] was cancelled the day before the event when Talita failed to make weight. A welterweight bout between [[Paul Daley]] and [[Derek Anderson (fighter)|Derek Anderson]] was also scrapped on the day of the event after Daley fell ill from effects of his [[weight cutting|weight cut]].{{cite web|url=http://www.mmafighting.com/2016/11/4/13522064/paul-daley-pulled-from-tonights-bellator-163-card-after-difficult|title=Paul Daley pulled from tonight's Bellator 163 card after difficult weight cut|publisher=mmafighting.com|author=Ariel Helwani|date=2016-11-04|access-date=2016-11-04}} Additionally, a catchweight bout at 160 pounds between Keenan Raymond and Kastroit Xhema was cancelled when Raymond withdrew from the fight.\n\nThe preliminary card featured the Bellator debut of [http://www.sherdog.com/fighter/Vinicius-de-Jesus-133401 Vinicius De Jesus]. It also featured the professional MMA debuts of former standout wrestlers [[Ed Ruth]] and Tyrell Fortune. Ruth was a three-time NCAA Division I champion for Penn State, while Fortune won an NCAA Division II title for Grand Canyon.\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent \u20aa3,081,813 (ILS)\n$803,980 (USD) \n|city=[[Tel Aviv, Israel]]\n}}\n\n'''Bellator 164: Koreshkov vs. Lima 2''' was held on November 10, 2016, at the [[Menora Mivtachim Arena]] in [[Tel Aviv, Israel]]. The event aired on [[Spike TV]] on tape delay.\n\n'''Background '''\n\nThe event was headlined by two of the world's top Welterweights. Bellator champion [[Andrey Koreshkov]] met former champion Bellator [[Douglas Lima]] in a rematch in the main event. Koreshkov won the welterweight title with a unanimous decision victory over Lima at Bellator 140. He defended the belt earlier that year with a dominant win over former [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] lightweight champion [[Benson Henderson]] at Bellator 153. Lima won the vacant welterweight title with a second-round TKO of [[Rick Hawn]] at Bellator 117. After a lengthy layoff, he fought Koreshkov and lost via unanimous decision. After his loss to Koreshkov, he was out for a full year, but came back in July to defeat [[Paul Daley]] at Bellator 158.\n\nIn addition, the card featured one of Israel's own in the co-headliner, when newly signed Bellator MMA featherweight and [[State of Israel|Israeli]] Army veteran [[Noad Lahat]] met NCAA Division II All-American [[Scott Cleve]], defeating him via a rear naked choke.\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Welterweight\n|[[Douglas Lima]]\n|def.\n|[[Andrey Koreshkov]] (c)\n|KO (punch)\n|3\n|1:21\n|For the [[List of
