The event aired live in prime time on [[Spike TV]].\n\n'''Background '''\n\nThe event was headlined by two of the world's top lightweights as two-time Bellator champion [[Michael Chandler]] met former [[World Extreme Cagefighting]] and [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] champion [[Benson Henderson]]. Chandler looked to defend his belt for the first time since defeating [[Patricky Freire]] via knockout at [[Bellator MMA in 2016#Bellator 157|Bellator 157: Dynamite 2]]. A 15-fight veteran of [[Bellator MMA]], Chandler has collected memorable wins at 155-pounds including a victory over former [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] lightweight champion [[Eddie Alvarez]]. Henderson earned a title shot in the lightweight division against its current titleholder in Chandler after defeating [[Patricio Freire]] at Bellator 160.\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event was headlined by a title fight rematch as [[Eduardo Dantas]] defended the [[List of Bellator champions#Bantamweight World Championship|Bellator Bantamweight Championship]] against former champion [[Joe Warren (fighter)|Joe Warren]]. Dantas had won back to back fights since losing the Bellator bantamweight title to Warren at Bellator 128 in 2014. Warren was coming off a submission win against Sirwan Kakai at Bellator 161.\n\nA fight between featherweight prospects [[A.J. McKee]] and [[Emmanuel Sanchez]] was scheduled for the co-main event. However, Sanchez pulled out in late November due to injury and was replaced by Ray Wood. The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nBellator 167 was originally scheduled to be headlined by a rematch between [[Patricky Freire]] and [[Derek Campos]]. The pair previously fought at Bellator 117 with Freire winning by TKO in the second round. However, on November 25, it was announced that Freire pulled out of the bout due to injury.\n\nBellator 167 was instead headlined by a bantamweight fight pitting [[Darrion Caldwell]] against [[Joe Taimanglo]]. Caldwell and Taimanglo previously met in a catchweight bout at Bellator 159. Caldwell did well in the first two rounds, but was caught with a fight-ending guillotine choke nine seconds into the third round. The defeat was the first loss of Caldwell's career and Caldwell was a 14-1 favorite entering the bout, making the upset the fourth biggest in MMA history. Taimanglo was riding a four-fight winning streak into the rematch. Caldwell came into the first bout with Taimanglo off a career-best win over Joe Warren at Bellator 151.\n\nA featherweight bout between [[Pat Curran (fighter)|Pat Curran]] and [[John Teixeira]] was also scheduled for this card. However, the fight was cancelled in early November due to an injury sustained by Curran. Teixeira instead faced [[Justin Lawrence (fighter)|Justin Lawrence]].\n\n'''Results'''\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Bantamweight\n|[[Darrion Caldwell]]\n|def.\n|[[Joe 8,113\n|gate= 862,006\u20ac (ITL)\n$981,784 (USD)\n}}\n'''Bellator 168: Sakara vs Beltran''' will be held on December 10, 2016, at the [[Nelson Mandela Forum]] in [[Florence, Italy]]. The event will air live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nIn the main event, [[Alessio Sakara]] faces [[Joey Beltran]]. Sakara made his Bellator debut earlier this year at the first Bellator event in Italy and defeated Brian Rogers by knockout in the second round.\n\nThe event was originally expected to be headlined by a rematch between [[Rafael Carvalho]] and [[Melvin Manhoef]] for the [[List of Bellator champions#Middleweight World Championship|Bellator Middleweight Championship]]. The pair previously fought at Bellator 155 with Carvalho retaining his title due to a controversial split decision. Bellator announcer Jimmy Smith called it one of the worst decisions he had ever seen in the promotion; likewise 5 of 5 media outlets scored the bout in favor of Manhoef.{{cite news|url=http://mmadecisions.com/decision/7009/Rafael-Carvalho-vs-Melvin-Manhoef|title=Rafael Carvalho def. Melvin Manhoef|publisher=MMA Decisions|access-date=2016-05-21}} However, on December 2, Carvalho pulled out of the match due to injury.\n\nThe event will also feature ''Bellator Kickboxing'' bouts including an anticipated female flyweight rematch between Denise Kielholtz and Gloria Peritore, the woman who defeated her this past June. The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event was headlined by a heavyweight bout between former [[List of Strikeforce champions#Light Heavyweight Championship|Strikeforce Light Heavyweight Champion]] and [[Rizin Fighting Federation 2#Rizin 2015 Heavyweight Grand Prix bracket|Rizin Heavyweight Grand Prix Champion]] [[Muhammed Lawal]] and Japanese Olympic gold medalist [[Satoshi Ishii]]. Lawal won the two-night, eight-man tournament at [[Rizin Fighting Federation]] on New Year's Eve in Japan. A 2008 Olympic gold medalist in judo, Ishii began his MMA career in December 2009 and made his Bellator debut in June 2016 against [[Rampage Jackson|Quinton Jackson]] at [[Bellator 157|Bellator 157: Dynamite 2]].\n\nBellator 169 is a Bellator MMA and [[BAMMA]] co-promoted event with the [[BAMMA Events#BAMMA 27: Duquesnoy vs. Philpott|BAMMA 27]] show filling out the rest of the card. Several top Irish prospects including Dylan Tuke, Ryan Curtis, Rhys McKee, and James Gallagher were featured on the card.\n\n'''Results'''\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent [[2016 in Bellator MMA|2016]]\n| followed_by = [[2018 in Bellator MMA|2018]]\n}}\n\n'''2017 in Bellator MMA''' was the tenth year in the history of [[Bellator MMA]], a [[mixed martial arts]] promotion based in the United States. Bellator held '''26 events''' in 2017.\n\n==Background==\nThis year, Bellator announced their first MMA event to be held in [[New York City|New York]]: Bellator NYC.[https://www.bellator.com/articles/m5rn8v/madison-square-garden-to-host-bellator-nyc-sonnen-vs-silva-pay-per-view-event-on-saturday-june-24 MADISON SQUARE GARDEN TO HOST BELLATOR NYC: SONNEN VS. SILVA PAY-PER-VIEW EVENT ON SATURDAY, JUNE 24, March 23, 2017] The event would also mark the Bellator debuts of former [[UFC]] commentator [[Mike Goldberg]], calling his first card on [[Spike TV]] since 2011 (which was the televised portion of Bellator NYC, referred to as Bellator 180), and former [[Strikeforce (mixed martial arts)|Strikeforce]] commentator [[Mauro Ranallo]].[https://www.bellator.com/articles/hu120v/bellator-signs-veteran-commentators-mike-goldberg-and-mauro-ranallo Bellator Signs Veteran Commentators Mike Goldberg and Mauro Ranallo, June 13, 2017]\n\n==Bellator 170==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator 170: Ortiz vs. Sonnen\n|image=\n|image_size=320px\n|date=January 21, 2017\n|venue=[[The Forum (Inglewood, California)|The Forum]]\n|attendance= 11,972 \n|gate= $1,134,963 \n|city=[[Inglewood, California]]\n}}\n'''Bellator 170: Ortiz vs. Sonnen ''' took place on January 21, 2017, at The Forum in Inglewood, California. The event aired live in prime time on Spike TV, drawing 1.4 million viewers.[https://mmapayout.com/2017/01/bellator-170-1-374m-viewers-on-spike-tv/ Bellator 170: 1.374M viewers on Spike TV] \u2013 MMA Payout, January 24, 2017\n\n'''Background'''\n\nOn October 18, 2016, it was announced that former [[List of UFC champions#Light Heavyweight Championship|UFC Light Heavyweight Champion]] [[Tito Ortiz]] and [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] veteran [[Chael Sonnen]] would headline this event.{{cite web|url=https://mmajunkie.com/2016/10/chael-sonnen-vs-tito-ortiz-set-for-jan-21-in-california|title=Chael Sonnen vs. Tito Ortiz set for Jan. 21 in California as Bellator 170 headliner}} Sonnen owns career wins over the likes of [[Yushin Okami]], [[Nate Marquardt]], [[Brian Stann]], former [[List of UFC champions#Light Heavyweight Championship|UFC Light Heavyweight Champion]] [[Maur\u00edcio Rua]] and former [[UFC Middleweight Championship|UFC Middleweight Champion]] [[Michael Bisping]]. Ortiz is a [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] Hall of Famer and one of the most decorated champions in UFC history. \"The Huntington Beach Bad Boy\" signed with Bellator in 2013 and has gone 2\u20131 with the promotion. He has wins over the likes of [[Alexander Shlemenko]], [[Stephan Bonnar]], [[Wanderlei Silva]], [[Ken Shamrock]] and [[Forrest Griffin]].\n\nA women's bout between Rebecca Ruth and [[Colleen Schneider]] was initially announced for this card. However, the bout never came to fruition for undisclosed reasons and Ruth was replaced by Chrissie Daniels\n\n'''Results'''\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Light California]]\n}}\n'''Bellator 172: Thomson vs. Pitbull''' aired on Saturday, February 18, 2017, at the [[SAP Center]] in [[San Jose, California]]. The event aired live in prime time on [[Spike TV]].\n\n'''Background '''\n\nThe event was scheduled to be headlined by heavyweight legend [[Fedor Emelianenko]] against former [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] veteran [[Matt Mitrione]]. Emelianenko retired in 2012, but ultimately returned to the sport in 2015. This was to be Emelianenko's first fight in the U.S. since 2011. Mitrione, a 38-year-old former NFL player has scored back-to-back knockout victories since joining Bellator over Carl Seumanutafa and [[Oli Thompson]]. Hours before the event, the fight was cancelled due to Mitrione becoming ill. As a result, [[Josh Thomson]] vs. [[Patricky Pitbull]] was moved up to the main event.\n\n'''Results'''\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Lightweight\n|[[Patricky Pitbull]]\n|def.\n|[[Josh Thomson]]\n|KO (punch)\n|2\n|0:40\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Heavyweight\n|[[Cheick Kongo]]\n|def.\n|[[Oli Thompson]]\n|Decision (unanimous) (30\u201326, 30\u201325, 30\u201325)\n|3\n|5:00\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Catchweight (187 lb)\n|[[Anatoly Tokov]]\n|def.\n|Francisco France \n|TKO (punches)\n|2\n|2:24\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Women's Flyweight\n|Veta Arteaga\n|def.\n|Brooke Mayo\n|TKO (doctor stoppage)\n|3\n|4:04\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Welterweight\n|Mauricio Alonso\n|def.\n|[[Josh Koscheck]]\n|TKO (punches)\n|1\n|4:42\n}}\n{{MMAevent card|Preliminary card (Spike.com)|header=no}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Lightweight\n|Nikko Jackson\n|def.\n|Cesar Gonzalez\n|Decision (unanimous) (29\u201328, 30\u201327, 30\u201327)\n|3\n|5:00\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Catchweight (166 lb)\n|J.J. Arena]]\n|attendance= 9,010\n|gate= $721,633 \n|city=[[Uncasville, Connecticut]]\n}}\n'''Bellator 178: Straus vs. Pitbull 4''' took place on April 21, 2017, at [[Mohegan Sun Arena]] in [[Uncasville, Connecticut]] . The event aired live on [[Spike TV]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nA [[List of Bellator MMA champions#Featherweight World Championship|Bellator Featherweight Championship]] tetralogy bout between current champion [[Daniel Straus (fighter)|Daniel Straus]] and former champion [[Patr\u00edcio Pitbull]] took place at the event. The pairing first met in a non-title bout at [[2011 in Bellator MMA#Bellator 45|Bellator 45]] on May 11, 2011, where Pitbull won by unanimous decision. Their second meeting took place at [[2015 in Bellator MMA#Bellator 132|Bellator 132]] on January 16, 2015, where Pitbull defended the title by submission in the fourth round. Their third meeting took place at [[2015 in Bellator MMA#Bellator 145|Bellator 145]] on November 6, 2015, where Straus captured the title by unanimous decision.\n\nA middleweight bout between [[Ed Ruth]] and Aaron Goodwine was originally scheduled for this card, but failed to materialize. [[Charlotte Motor Speedway]] in [[Concord, North Carolina]]\n\n'''Background'''\n\nOn May 1, 2017, Bellator announced a special four-fight card that took place at the [[Monster Energy NASCAR All-Star Race]] XXXIII. The goal of the event was to scout new talent for a prospective contract. Unlike all previous Bellator events, this event was not televised, as this event took place at a NASCAR race, where [[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]], which holds rights to [[Fox UFC|a rival MMA promotion]], holds video rights for events at the Charlotte Motor Speedway during the event.\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout \n|Heavyweight\n|[[Allen Crowder]]\n|def.\n|Robert Neal \n|TKO (punches)\n|1\n|2:24\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout \n|Welterweight\n|Jacob McClintock\n|def.\n|Jeremie Holloway\n|Submission (guillotine choke)\n|1\n|1:39\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout \n|Lightweight\n|Lashawn Alcocks\n|def.\n|Mike Stevens\n|TKO (punches)\n|1\n|2:20\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout \n|Light Heavyweight\n|Allen Bose\n|def.\n|Chris Crawford\n|Decision (unanimous) (29\u201328, 29\u201328, 29\u201328)\n|3\n|3:00\n| \n}}\n{{MMAevent end|notes=yes}}\n{{cite web|url=https://www.sherdog.com/news/news/Bellator-MMA-Reveals-FourBout-Lineup-for-NASCAR-AllStar-Race-Weekend-on-May-20-120915|title=Bellator MMA Reveals Four Bout Lineup for NASCAR AllStar Race Weekend |date=May 19, 2017|website=sherdog.com|last=Critchfield|first=Tristen}}\n\n==Bellator NYC/Bellator 180==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator NYC: Sonnen vs. Silva / Bellator 180\n|image=\n|image_size=\n|date=June 24, 2017\n|venue=[[Madison Square Garden]]\n|attendance= 12,133\n|gate= $1,630,314\n|buyrate= 130,000{{Cite web|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2017/7/20/16002482/estimated-pay-per-view-numbers-are-in-for-ufc-213-bellator-nyc|title = Estimated PPV numbers are in for UFC 213, Bellator NYC|date = July 20, 2017}}\n|city=New York City\n}}\n'''Bellator NYC: Sonnen vs. Silva''' and '''Bellator 180''' took place on June 24, 2017, at [[Madison Square Garden]] in New York City. The event aired both Spike TV and on [[Pay-per-view|PPV]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nA grudge match between rivals [[Chael Sonnen]] and [[Wanderlei Silva]] served as the main event.{{cite news|url=https://mmajunkie.com/2017/03/chael-sonnen-vs-wanderlei-silva-to-headline-bellator-180-ppv-event-at-madison-square-garden|title=Chael Sonnen vs. Wanderlei Silva to headline Bellator 180 PPV event at Madison Square Garden|publisher=mmajunkie.com|author=Steven Marrocco|date=March 20, 2017|access-date=2017-03-20}}\n\nThe co-main event was a heavyweight bout between [[Fedor Emelianenko]] vs. [[Matt Mitrione]]. The pairing were supposed to meet at Bellator 172 but Mitrione had to be hospitalized due to kidney stones.{{cite news|url=http://www.mmaweekly.com/fedor-emelianenko-vs-matt-mitrione-joins-sonnen-vs-silva-on-bellator-ppv|title=Fedor Emelianenko vs. Matt Mitrione Joins Sonnen vs. Silva on Bellator PPV|publisher=mmaweekly.com|author=Staff|date=March 21, 2017|access-date=2017-03-21}}\n\nDebuting former UFC fighter [[Ryan Bader]] was initially scheduled to face [[Muhammed Lawal]] on this card. However, Lawal pulled out of the fight due to an injury and Bader instead faced Light Heavyweight champion [[Phil Davis (fighter)|Phil Davis]] in a rematch.{{cite news|url=https://mmajunkie.com/2017/04/phil-davis-vs-ryan-bader-title-fight-bellator-180-king-mo-lawal-out|title=Phil Davis replaces 'King Mo' Lawal, will defend title vs. Ryan Bader at Bellator 180|publisher=mmajunkie.com|author=MMA Junkie Staff|date=April 24, 2017|access-date=2017-04-27}} Bader and Davis first met at [[UFC on Fox: Gustafsson vs. Johnson]] on January 24, 2015, with Bader winning by split decision.\n\nA fight between Keri Anne Melendez and Sadee Monseratte Williams was scheduled but cancelled after Melendez pulled out due to injury.{{cite web|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2017/6/12/15785770/keri-melendez-out-of-bellator-180-heather-hardy-vs-alice-yauger-moves-to-spike-card|title=Keri Melendez out of Bellator 180, Heather Hardy vs. Alice Yauger moves to Spike card |date=June 12, 2017|publisher=mmafighting.com|author=Marc Raimondi|access-date=2017-06-12}}\n\nThe PPV portion of the MSG card was referred to as Bellator NYC. The event aired live on [[Spike TV]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nBellator 185 marked the debut of heralded middleweight fighter [[Gegard Mousasi]]. Having competed for the [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] for the last four years, Mousasi opted to sign with Bellator MMA when his contract came up.\n\n[[Muhammed Lawal]] was scheduled to face [[Liam McGeary]] in a Light Heavyweight bout in the co-main event. However, on October 2, he pulled out of the fight due to an undisclosed injury. He was replaced by [[Bubba McDaniel]].{{cite web|url=https://www.sherdog.com/news/news/Bubba-McDaniel-Replaces-King-Mo-Meets-Liam-McGeary-at-Bellator-185-on-Oct-20-127327|title=Bubba McDaniel Replaces 'King Mo,' Meets Liam McGeary at Bellator 15 on Oct. 20}} The following week, McGeary pulled out of the fight due to a thumb injury.\n\n[[Brennan Ward]] was scheduled to face [[David Rickels]] in a welterweight bout on the main card. However, on October 16, Ward was removed from the card due to injury and Rickels was pulled from the card as a result.\n\nJavier Torres was scheduled to face [[Neiman Gracie]] on this card, but pulled out due to injury. MMA|2019]]\n}}\n\n'''2018 in Bellator MMA''' was the tenth year in the history of [[Bellator MMA]], a [[mixed martial arts]] promotion based in the United States. Bellator held '''23 events''' in 2018.\n\n==Background==\nIn addition to airing cards on the newly-rebranded [[Paramount Network]] (formally Spike), Bellator would sign a multi-year deal with streaming service [[DAZN]]. Their partnership began with Bellator 206, which was broadcast exclusively on DAZN. Bellator would hold its 200th numbered event on May 25, 2018.\n\n==Bellator Heavyweight World Grand Prix Tournament==\nIn 2018, Bellator organised the 2018\u20132019 Heavyweight Grand Prix that will crown the Bellator Heavyweight champion.{{Cite news|url=http://mmajunkie.com/2017/11/bellator-makes-2018-heavyweight-grand-prix-official-check-out-the-new-poster|title=Bellator makes 2018 heavyweight grand prix official \u2013 check out the new poster|date=2017-11-14|work=MMAjunkie|access-date=2017-11-21|language=en-US}} This belt was vacated in May 2016 by [[Vitaly Minakov]]. The event aired live in prime time on Paramount Network.\n\n'''Background'''\n\n[[Rafael Lovato Jr.]] was originally scheduled to face [[John Salter]] on this card. However, Salter was pulled by the Illinois Athletic Commission due to an eye issue on April 24 and replaced by [[Gerald Harris (fighter)|Gerald Harris]]. The event aired on tape delay in prime time on Paramount Network.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThis card was expected to be headlined by a rematch between [[Mirko Cro Cop]] and [[Roy Nelson (fighter)|Roy Nelson]]. The pair previously fought in October 2011 at [[UFC 137]] with Nelson winning by TKO. The bout was also expected to serve as an alternate bout for the 2018 Bellator Heavyweight World Grand Prix Tournament. However, the bout was scrapped during the week leading up to the event as Cro Cop pulled out of the fight citing an injury.{{cite The event aired live on [[Paramount Network]] and [[DAZN]].{{Cite news|url=http://mmadna.nl/john-teixeira-valt-in-voor-pat-curran-tegen-aj-mckee-tijdens-bellator-20|title=John Teixeira valt in voor Pat Curran tegen AJ McKee tijdens Bellator 205|last=DNA|first=MMA|date=2018-08-13|work=MMA DNA|access-date=2018-09-22|language=en-US}}\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event was expected to see a featherweight main event featuring [[A.J. McKee instead faced [[John Teixeira|John Macap\u00e1]].\n\nGoiti Yamaguchi was expected to fight [[Patricky Freire]] on the card but pulled out before the fight due to injury. 206==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator 206: Mousasi vs. MacDonald\n|image=\n|date= September 29, 2018\n|venue= [[SAP Center]]\n|city= [[San Jose, California]]\n|attendance= 12,609\n|gate= $1,248,291\n|purse=\n}}\n\n'''Bellator 206: Mousasi vs. MacDonald''' took place on September 29, 2018 at the [[SAP Center]] in [[San Jose, California]]. The event streamed live on [[DAZN]] in the United States and all other regions previously served by the service, including Austria, Canada, Germany, Italy, Switzerland, and Japan, as part of a new agreement giving the service rights to seven exclusive cards per-year.{{Cite news|url=https://variety.com/2018/tv/news/viacom-bellator-mma-1202857974/|title=Viacom\u2019s Bellator MMA Signs Multi-Year Deal With OTT Service DAZN|last=Holloway|first=Daniel|date=26 June 2018|work=Variety|access-date=27 June 2018}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2018/6/26/17505834/bellator-announces-broadcast-deal-with-streaming-service-dazn|title=Bellator announces broadcast deal with streaming service DAZN|work=MMA Fighting|access-date=27 June 2018}}\n\nIn the United Kingdom, Bellator 206 was televised by Viacom-owned [[Channel 5 (UK)|Channel 5]], but the telecast ceased transmission at 6:00 a.m. (in favour of [[Milkshake!|preschool programming]]) before the main event, due to [[Watershed (broadcasting)|watershed]] regulations.{{Cite news|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2018/9/30/17919330/officials-explain-why-uk-fans-ended-up-watching-peppa-pig-instead-of-bellator-206-main-event|title=Officials explain why UK fans ended up watching \u2018Peppa Pig\u2019 instead of Bellator 206 main event|work=MMA Fighting|access-date=2018-10-01}}\n\n===Background===\n\nThe event featured a [[List of Bellator MMA champions#Middleweight World Championship|Bellator Middleweight Champion]] bout between the champion [[Gegard Mousasi]] and current [[List of Bellator MMA champions#Welterweight World Championship|Bellator Welterweight Champion]] [[Rory MacDonald (fighter)|Rory MacDonald]]. MacDonald was attempting to become the second multi-division champion in Bellator history, after former Bellator bantamweight and featherweight champion [[Joe Warren (fighter)|Joe Warren]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2018/6/21/17489524/gegard-mousasi-to-defend-bellator-middleweight-title-against-rory-macdonald-in-september|title=Gegard Mousasi to defend Bellator middleweight title against Rory MacDonald in September|work=MMA Fighting|access-date=2018-09-22}}\n\nIn addition, former UFC light heavyweight champion [[Rampage Jackson|Quinton Jackson]] met rival and former [[PRIDE FC]] middleweight champion [[Wanderlei Silva]] for the fourth time in their respective careers. Going into this fight, Silva held a 2\u20131 advantage in the series.{{Cite news|url=https://mmasucka.com/2018/06/26/wanderlei-silva-vs-quinton-jackson-4-to-be-contested-at-heavyweight-on-september-29/|title=Wanderlei Silva vs. Quinton Jackson 4 to be contested at heavyweight on September 29 - MMASucka.com|last=Skytte|first=Mike|date=2018-06-26|work=MMASucka.com|access-date=2018-09-22|language=en-US|archive-date=2018-09-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180922102100/https://mmasucka.com/2018/06/26/wanderlei-silva-vs-quinton-jackson-4-to-be-contested-at-heavyweight-on-september-29/|url-status=dead}}\n\nThis event featured the start of Bellator's inaugural welterweight grand prix tournament. Fighters expected to participate in the tournament are [[Rory MacDonald (fighter)|Rory MacDonald]], [[Jon Fitch]], [[Douglas Lima]], [[Andrey Koreshkov]], [[Paul Daley]], [[Michael Page (fighter)|Michael Page]], [[Neiman Gracie]], [[Ed Ruth]], [[Lorenz Larkin]], and [[Erick Silva]], who replaced Yaroslav Amosov.{{Cite news|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ca/mma/news/bellator-welterweight-grand-prix-michael-page-vs-paul-daley-rory-macdonald-jon-fitch-dazn/1nr7cj0dwbxy01ije7q2jvoc1a|title=SN exclusive: Bellator welterweight grand prix is set, highlighted by Page vs. Daley grudge match|date=2018-08-06|work=Sporting News|access-date=2018-09-22}}\n\nDon Mohammed and Salvador Becerra were scheduled to face each other in a Lightweight bout on the undercard. However, the bout was cancelled the week of the fight for undisclosed reasons.{{Cite news|url=https://www.tapology.com/fightcenter/events/53925-bellator-mousasi-vs-macdonald|title=Bellator 206: Mousasi vs. MacDonald \u2013 Cancelled & Fizzled Bouts|date=2018-09-28|work=Tapology|access-date=2018-09-30|language=en-US}}\n\nAt weight-ins, Ricky Abdelaziz weighed in at 147.3 pounds, 1.3 pounds over the featherweight non-title fight upper limit of 146 pounds. As a result, the bout proceeded catchweight. Abdelaziz was fined 20 percent of his purse which 10% went to his opponent, Laird Anderson, and 10% went to [[California State Athletic Commission]].{{Cite news|url=https://mmajunkie.com/2018/09/bellator-206-san-jose-gegard-mousasi-rory-macdonald-weigh-in-results-live-video-stream|title=Bellator 206 weigh-in results: Mousasi, MacDonald official for superfight title bout|date=2018-09-28|work=MMAjunkie|access-date=2018-09-30|language=en-US}} The bout between DeMarco Villalona and Abraham Vaesau was cancelled after Villalona did not make weight.\n\n=== Results ===\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Middleweight\n|[[Gegard Mousasi]] (c)\n|def.\n|[[Rory MacDonald (fighter)|Rory MacDonald]]\n|TKO (punches The event was live on [[Paramount Network]] and [[DAZN]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event featured a [[List of Bellator champions|Bellator Lightweight Championship]] bout between the champion [[Brent Primus]] and former champion [[Michael Chandler]].{{cite web|url=http://mmajunkie.com/2017/06/bellator-nyc-brent-primus-breaks-michael-chandlers-leg-wins-lightweight-title|title=Bellator NYC results: Brent Primus wins lightweight title with injury TKO over Michael Chandler|publisher=mmajunkie.com|author=Steven Marrocco|date=June 24, 2017}} The rematch was scheduled for Bellator 197, but Primus pulled out due to injury.\n\nA women's flyweight bout between former title contender [[Alejandra Lara]] and [[Juliana Velasquez]] was also announced for the card.{{Cite news|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2018/10/11/17963972/alejandra-lara-returns-at-bellator-212-in-hawaii-meets-unbeaten-juliana-velasquez|title=Alejandra Lara returns at Bellator 212 in Hawaii, meets unbeaten Juliana Velasquez|date=2018-10-11|work=MMA Fighting|access-date=2018-10-16|language=en-US}}\n\nOn November 19, 2018, it was announced Sam Sicilia will face Derek Campos at this event.{{Cite news|url=https://fansided.com/2018/11/19/sam-sicilia-versus-derek-campos-added-to-bellator-212/|title=Bellator 212: Sam Sicilia vs. Derek Campos added to main card|date=2018-11-19|work=FanSided|access-date=2018-11-20|language=en-US}}\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Lightweight\n|[[Michael Chandler]] \n|def.\n|[[Brent Primus]] (c)\n|Decision (unanimous) (50\u201345, 50\u201345, 50\u201345)\n|5\n|5:00\n|For the [[List of Bellator champions|Bellator Lightweight Championship]].\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Heavyweight\n|[[Javy Ayala]]\n|def.\n|[[Frank Mir]]\n|TKO (submission to punches)\n|2\n|4:30\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Featherweight\n|[[A.J. He advanced to fight [[Neiman Gracie]].\n\n{{Clear}}\n\n==Bellator 214==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator 214: Fedor vs. Bader\n|image=\n|image_size=320px\n|date=January 26, 2019\n|venue=[[The Forum (Inglewood, California)|The Forum]]\n|attendance= 12,914\n|gate= $1,277,196\n|city=[[Inglewood, California]]\n}}\n\n'''Bellator 214: Fedor vs. Bader''' took place on January 26, 2019 at [[The Forum (Inglewood, California)|The Forum]] in [[Inglewood, California]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/boxing/la-sp-boxing-newsletter-20181002-story.html|title=Bellator heavyweight grand prix will conclude at the Forum|date=2018-10-02|newspaper=LA Times|access-date=2018-10-16|language=en-US}} The event aired live on [[Paramount Network]] and [[DAZN]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThis event concluded the [[2018 in Bellator MMA#Bellator Heavyweight World Grand Prix Tournament|Bellator Heavyweight World Grand Prix]] by awarding the winner of the main event with the Bellator Heavyweight World Championship. This belt was vacated in May 2016 by [[Vitaly Minakov]], who had not defended the title since April 2014. [[Fedor Emelianenko]] and current Bellator Light Heavyweight World Champion [[Ryan Bader]] both advanced to the finals.{{Cite news|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/mma/fedor-stops-sonnen-bellator-208-meets-bader-grand-prix-final/|title=Fedor stops Sonnen at Bellator 208, meets Bader in Grand Prix final|date=2018-10-15|work=Sportsnet|access-date=2018-10-16|language=en-US}}\n\nA featherweight bout between elite prospects [[Aaron Pico]] and Henry Corrales was announced for the event on November 7, 2018.{{Cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/boxing/la-sp-bellator-pico-20181107-story.html|title=Whittier's Aaron Pico lands on Bellator card at the Forum|date=2018-11-07|newspaper=LA Times|access-date=2018-11-09|language=en-US}}\n\nOn November 19, 2018, it was announced that [[List of Bellator MMA champions#Middleweight World Championship|Bellator Middleweight World Champion]] [[Gegard Mousasi]] would be defending the title against [[Rafael Lovato Jr.]] in the co main event.{{cite web|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2018/11/19/18103828/gegard-mousasi-vs-rafael-lovato-jr-set-for-bellator-214|title=Gegard Mousasi vs Rafael Lovato Jr. booked for Bellator 214|work=MMAFighting.com|date=November 19, 2018}} However, Mousasi pulled out on December 19 due to back injury and Lovato was eventually pulled from the card.{{cite web|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2018/12/20/18150798/gegard-mousasi-injured-out-bellator-214-title-fight-rafael-lovato-jr|title=Gegard Mousasi injured, out of Bellator 214 title fight with Rafael Lovato Jr.|work=MMAFighting.com|date=December 19, 2018}}\n\nOn December 3, 2018, it was announced that Bellator 214 would feature the MMA debut of former WWE [[World Heavyweight Champion (WWE)|World [[DAZN]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event was to feature a featherweight main event bout between [[Emmanuel Sanchez]] and Ashleigh Grimshaw;{{Cite news|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2018/11/30/18120641/emmanuel-sanchez-vs-ashleigh-grimshaw-to-headline-bellator-event-on-march-22|title=Emmanuel Sanchez vs. Ashleigh Grimshaw to headline Bellator event on March 22|date=2018-11-30|work=mmafighting.com|access-date=2018-12-04|language=en-US}} However, the promotion announced that March 8 that [[Georgi Karakhanyan]] replaced Grimshaw due to undisclosed reasons. The two previous met at [[Bellator MMA in 2017|Bellator 170]] where Sanchez won by a close decision.\n\nA Light Heavyweight bout between Christian Edwards and Roman Huerta was cancelled the day of the weigh-in. Huerta did not weigh in as he was reportedly more than five pounds heavier than Edwards.{{Cite The event aired on [[Paramount Network]] and [[DAZN]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event was expected to feature a welterweight bout between [[Andrey Koreshkov]] and [[Lorenz Larkin]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.mmajunkie.com/2018/12/andrey-koreshkov-vs-lorenz-larkin-headlines-bellator-event-march-29/amp|title=Andrey Koreshkov vs. Lorenz Larkin headlines Bellator event on March 29|date=2018-12-13|work=mmajunkie.com|access-date=2018-12-13|language=en-US}} However, Larkin pulled out on March 1 due to undisclosed reasons.{{Cite news|url=https://www.mmajunkie.com/2019/03/lorenz-larkin-out-bellator-219-headliner-andrey-koreshkov-injury/amp|title=Lorenz Larkin says he's out of Bellator 219 headliner vs. Andrey Koreshkov|date=2019-03-01|work=mmajunkie.com|access-date=2019-03-01|language=en-US}} Koreshkov remained on the card facing Michael Jasper.{{Cite news|url=https://www.mmajunkie.com/2019/03/bellator-219-andrey-koreshkov-vs-newcomer-mike-jasper/amp|title=Andrey Koreshkov draws newcomer Mike Jasper at Bellator 219|date=2019-03-05|work=mmajunkie.com|access-date=2019-03-05|language=en-US}}\n\nA lightweight bout between [[Saad Awad]] and [[Brandon Girtz]] was announced as the new main event.{{Cite news|url=https://www.mmajunkie.com/2019/03/ex-champ-daniel-straus-returns-at-bellator-219-saad-awad-vs-brandon-girtz-set-as-headliner/amp|title=Ex-champ Daniel Straus returns at Bellator 219; 225==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator 225: Mitrione vs. Kharitonov 2\n|image=\n|image_size=\n|date=August 24, 2019\n|venue=[[Webster Bank Arena]]\n|attendance= 6,631\n|gate= $648,141\n|city=[[Bridgeport, Connecticut]]\n}}\n\n'''Bellator 225: Mitrione vs. Kharitonov 2''' was a [[mixed martial arts]] event that took place on August 24, 2019 at [[Webster Bank Arena]] in [[Bridgeport, Connecticut]]. The event took place on [[Paramount Network]] and [[DAZN]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThis marked the second major MMA event to take place in Connecticut proper, after [[CES MMA|CES]] 56, rather than on tribal or reservation land, and will be overseen by the Connecticut Boxing Commission.\n\nThe event featured a heavyweight rematch between [[Matt Mitrione]] and [[Sergei Kharitonov]]. The two met earlier in the year at Bellator 215 where the bout ended in a no contest 15 seconds into the bout due to an accidental groin kick.\n\n[[Vitaly Minakov]] was originally scheduled to face [[Javy Ayala]] on the card. However, the day of the event it was announced that Ayala was pulled from the fight by the Connecticut Boxing Commission due to an undisclosed medical reason; as a result [[Timothy Johnson (fighter)|Timothy Johnson]] moved up from a preliminary bout against Azunna Anyanwu to face Minakov in the co-main event.{{cite web|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2019/08/bellator-225-javy-ayala-out-vitaly-minakov-vs-tim-johnson-new-co-main/amp|title=Javy Ayala out of Bellator 225 co-headliner; Tim Johnson steps in to fight Vitaly Minakov|work=MMA Junkie|date=August 24, 2019|access-date=August 24, 2019|archive-date=September 27, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190927030539/https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2019/08/bellator-225-javy-ayala-out-vitaly-minakov-vs-tim-johnson-new-co-main/amp|url-status=dead}}\n\nBellator 225 became the first event in the organizational history where every bout ended via stoppage.{{cite web|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2019/08/bellator-225-post-event-facts-most-finishes-single-card-history-record|title=Bellator 225 post-event facts: History made with 14 fights and 14 The event marked the fourth event in Bellator's European series, with the Bellator Dublin portion of the card airing on [[Channel 5 (UK)|Channel 5]] in the [[UK]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe Bellator Dublin main event was original a bantamweight bout between James Gallagher and Cal Ellenor.{{cite web |title=James Gallagher faces Cal Ellenor at Bellator Dublin in September |url=https://www.mmafighting.com/platform/amp/2019/7/3/20680655/james-gallagher-faces-cal-ellenor-at-bellator-dublin-in-september? |website=mmafighting.com |access-date=2 July 2019}} However, Ellenor pulled out on September 16 due to injury.{{cite web |title=Cal Ellenor injured, out against James Gallagher of Bellator Dublin main event |url=https://www.mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2019/09/cal-ellenor-injured-james-gallagher-needs-bellator-europe-4-main-event/amp |website=mmajunkie.com |access-date=16 September 2019 |archive-date=2 October 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191002083717/https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2019/09/cal-ellenor-injured-james-gallagher-needs-bellator-europe-4-main-event/amp |url-status=dead }} Gallagher instead fought [[UFC]] veteran [[Roman Salazar]].{{cite web |title=Roman Salazar makes Bellator debut against James Gallagher at Bellator Dublin |url=https://www.mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2019/09/bellator-dublin-james-gallagher-gets-roman-salazar-replacement-opponent/amp |website=mmajunkie.com |access-date=19 September 2019 |archive-date=2 October 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191002082901/https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2019/09/bellator-dublin-james-gallagher-gets-roman-salazar-replacement-opponent/amp |url-status=dead }}\n\nThe fights billed as Bellator 227 took place on [[Paramount Network]] and [[DAZN]], with the headlining bout featuring former [[World Extreme Cagefighting|WEC]] and [[UFC Lightweight Championship|UFC Lightweight Champion]] [[Benson Henderson]] and [[Myles Jury]].{{cite web |title=Benson Henderson to meet Myles Jury in Bellator 227 headliner |url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2019/7/22/20704265/benson-henderson-to-meet-myles-jury-in-bellator-dublin-headliner |website=mmafighting.com |access-date=22 July 2019}}\n\n[[Brandon Girtz]] was expected to face Paul Redmond at the event. Redmond pulled out on September 4 due to injury. Girtz was instead to face Bellator newcomer [[Jon Tuck]].{{cite web |title=Paul Redmond injured, Brandon Girtz faces Jon Tuck at Bellator 227|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2019/9/4/20849102/injury-forces-paul-redmond-off-bellator-dublin-jon-tuck-steps-in-to-face-brandon-girtz |website=mmafighting.com |access-date=4 September 2019}} The bout was canceled after Girtz pulled out due to injury.{{cite web|title=Brandon Girtz injured; fight with Jon Tuck scratched from Bellator 227|url=https://www.mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2019/09/bellator-227-brandon-girtz-injured-co-headliner-scratched/amp|website=mmajunkie.com|access-date=26 September 2019|archive-date=22 September MacDonald vs. Lima 2''' took place on October 26, 2019 at [[Mohegan Sun Arena]] in [[Uncasville, Connecticut]]. The event aired on [[DAZN]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event featured the finals of the Bellator Welterweight World Grand Prix for the [[List of Bellator MMA champions#Welterweight World Championship|Bellator Welterweight World Championship]] between the champion [[Rory MacDonald (fighter)|Rory MacDonald]] and former champion [[Douglas Lima]].{{cite web |title=Mir-Nelson 2, MacDonald-Lima 2 headline Bellator 231, 232 on back-to-back nights in Connecticut |url=https://www.mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2019/08/frank-mir-roy-nelson-2-rory-macdonald-douglas-lima-2-bellator-230-231-connecticut/amp |website=mmajunkie.com |access-date=23 August 2019 |archive-date=24 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190924170623/https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2019/08/frank-mir-roy-nelson-2-rory-macdonald-douglas-lima-2-bellator-230-231-connecticut/amp |url-status=dead }} The two previously met at [[Bellator MMA in 2018|Bellator 192]] where MacDonald won by unanimous decision to claim the championship.\n\n[[Vitaly Minakov]] was expected to face [[Javy Ayala]] at the event.{{cite web |title=Vitaly Minakov vs. Javy Ayala re-booked for Bellator 232 |url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2019/9/24/20882078/vitaly-minakov-vs-javy-ayala-re-booked-for-bellator-232 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200625000000/https://udn.com/news/story/121424/4659358 |archive-date=25 June 2020 |access-date=24 September 2019 |website=mmafighting.com}} Eventually, Minakov pulled out due to visa issues and the bout was cancelled.{{cite web |title=Vitaly Minakov vs. Javy Ayala scrapped from Bellator 232 |url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2019/10/22/20927970/vitaly-minakov-javy-ayala-scrapped-bellator-232-mma |website=mmafighting.com|date=22 October 2019 |access-date=23 October 2019}}\n\nA Featherweight bout between [[Robin van Roosmalen]] and Cris Lencioni was scheduled for the main card. However, Van Roosmalen missed the featherweight limit by nine pounds and the bout was cancelled. Isaiah Chapman also came in one-quarter pound over the allotted bantamweight limit.{{cite web |title=Bellator 232 weigh-ins | url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2019/10/bellator-232-rory-macdonald-douglas-lima-weigh-in-results-live-video-stream |website=mmajunkie.com| date=25 October 2019 |access-date=October 25, 2019}}\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Welterweight\n|[[Douglas Lima]]\n|def.\n|[[Rory MacDonald (fighter)|Rory MacDonald]] (c)\n|Decision (unanimous) (49-46, 50-45, 50-45)\n|5\n|5:00\n|Bellator Welterweight World Grand Prix Final. (USD)\n|city=[[Saitama, Japan]]\n}}\n\n'''''Bellator Japan''''' (also known as '''''Bellator 237: Fedor vs. Rampage''''') was an event for [[Bellator MMA]] that took place on December 29, 2019 at [[Saitama Super Arena]] in [[Saitama, Japan]]. The event aired live on [[Paramount Network]] and [[DAZN]] in the United States. \n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event was announced by Bellator on October 9, 2019 as the company's debut in Japan. The event marked Bellator's first collaboration with the Japanese [[Rizin Fighting Federation]]; the preliminary matches featured Rizin fighters. The event was headlined by a heavyweight bout between former Pride FC Heavyweight Champion [[Fedor Emelianenko]] and former [[UFC Light Heavyweight Championship|UFC Light Heavyweight Champion]] [[Rampage Jackson|Quinton Jackson]].{{cite web|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2019/10/fedor-emelianenko-vs-rampage-jackson-to-headline-bellator-japan-on-dec-29|work=mmajunkie.com|title=Fedor Emelianenko vs. Rampage Jackson to headline Bellator Japan on Dec. 29|date=October 9, 2019}}\n\nA 160 pound catchweight bout between former [[List of Bellator MMA champions|Bellator Lightweight Champion]] [[Michael Chandler]] and former [[World Extreme Cagefighting|WEC]] and [[UFC Lightweight Champion]] [[Benson Henderson]] was expected to take place at the event.{{cite web |last1=Marrocco |first1=Steven |title=Michael Chandler vs. Benson Henderson 2 co-headlines Bellator Japan |url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2019/10/25/20933138/michael-chandler-vs-benson-henderson-2-co-headlines-bellator-japan |website=[[MMAFighting.com]] |date=25 October 2019 |access-date=5 December 2019}} It was to have been a rematch from [[Bellator MMA in 2016|Bellator 165]] where Chandler won by split decision over Henderson to remain the lightweight champion.{{cite web |last1=Dyce |first1=Mike |title=Bellator 165: Michael Chandler defeats Benson Henderson |url=https://www.si.com/mma/2016/11/20/bellator-165-michael-chandler-defeats-benson-henderson |website=[[SportsIllustrated.com]] |access-date=5 December 2019}} However, Henderson pulled out on December 5 due to injury. Chandler instead faced [[Sidney Outlaw]].{{cite web |last1=Bohn |first1=Mike |title=Benson Henderson out of Bellator 237; Sidney Outlaw steps in vs. Michael Chandler |url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2019/12/benson-henderson-out-bellator-237-japan-sidney-outlaw-in-michael-chandler |website=[[MMAJunkie.com]] |date=5 December 2019 |access-date=5 December [[2019 in Bellator MMA|2019]]\n| followed_by = [[2021 in Bellator MMA|2021]]\n}}\n\n'''2020 in Bellator MMA''' was the twelfth year in the history of [[Bellator MMA]], a [[mixed martial arts]] promotion based in the United States. Bellator held '''18 events''' in 2020.\n\n==Background==\nBecause of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], Bellator would go on hiatus after its 240th numbered event on February 22, 2020. The promotion would resume holding events with [[Bellator MMA in 2020#Bellator 242|Bellator 242]] on July 24.\n\nOn September 11, 2020, it was announced that Bellator telecasts would move to [[CBS Sports Network]], starting October 1, after Viacom's [[2019 merger of CBS and Viacom|re-merger]] with [[CBS Corporation]] in 2019.{{Cite web|last=Martin|first=Damon|date=2020-09-11|title=Bellator MMA announces move from Paramount Network to CBS Sports Network|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2020/9/11/21432619/bellator-mma-announces-move-from-paramount-network-to-cbs-sports-network|access-date=2020-09-12|website=MMA Fighting|language=en}} Prior to the announcement, CBS Sports Network debuted the recap series ''Bellator MMA: Recharged'' on April 25, 2020.[https://www.mmamania.com/2020/4/25/21228619/bellator-mma-recharged-on-cbs-sports-network-debuts-tonight-at-8-p-m-et Bellator MMA Recharged on CBS Sports Network debuts TONIGHT at 8 p.m. ET - MMAMania.com Apr 25, 2020][https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2020/04/bellator-recharged-premieres-cbs-sports-network \u2018Bellator Recharged\u2019 debuts Saturday on CBS Sports Network - mmajunkie; April 20, 2020]\n\nBellator 248, which was held on October 10, would be the first MMA event to be held by a major promotion in [[France]] since the sport was legalized in January.[http://www.bellator.com/articles/adp6hj/bellator-to-hold-first-major-mma-event-in-france-on-saturday-october-10-at-accor-arena-in-paris Bellator to Hold First Major MMA Event in France on Saturday, October 10 at Accor Arena in Paris]\n\n==Bellator Featherweight World Grand Prix Tournament==\n{{transcluded section|2019 in Bellator MMA#Bellator Featherweight World Grand Prix Tournament}}\n{{trim|{{#section-h:2019 in Bellator MMA|Bellator Featherweight World Grand Prix Tournament}}}}\n\n==Bellator 238==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator 238: Budd vs. Cyborg\n|image=\n|image_size=\n|date=January 25, 2020\n|venue=[[The Forum (Inglewood, California)|The Forum]]\n|attendance= 15,169\n|gate= 1,725,989\n|city=[[Inglewood, California]]\n}}\n\n'''Bellator 238: Budd vs. Cyborg''' took place on January 25, 2020 at [[The Forum (Inglewood, California)|The Forum]] in [[Inglewood, California]]. The event was to be headlined by a bantamweight bout between James Gallagher and Cal Ellenor.{{cite web |title=James Gallagher vs. Cal Ellenor rebooked for Bellator Dublin main event in February |url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2019/11/20/20973798/james-gallagher-vs-cal-ellenor-rebooked-for-main-event-at-bellator-dublin-in-february |website=mmafighting.com|access-date=21 November 2019}} However, on February 4, it was announced that Gallagher pulled out of the event due to a back injury, thus a women's featherweight bout between [[Leah McCourt]] and Judith Ruis was bumped to the main event.{{cite web |title=Injury rules James Gallagher out of Bellator Dublin; Leah McCourt vs. Judith Ruis moved to main event|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2020/2/4/21122038/injury-rules-james-gallagher-out-of-bellator-dublin-leah-mccourt-vs-judith-ruis-moved-to-main-event |website=mmafighting.com|date=4 February 2020 |access-date=4 February 2020}}\n\nThe fights billed as Bellator 240 will be held on tape-delay on [[Paramount Network]] and [[DAZN]] and will feature a lightweight bout between former [[List of Bellator MMA champions|Bellator Lightweight World Champion]] [[Brent Primus]] and Peter Queally.{{cite web |title=Brent Primus vs. Peter Queally booked to Bellator Europe 7 |url=https://www.mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2019/12/bellator-dublin-brent-primus-vs-peter-queally-booked-co-main-event/amp |website=mmafighting.com |access-date=11 December 2019 |archive-date=13 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191213042201/https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2019/12/bellator-dublin-brent-primus-vs-peter-queally-booked-co-main-event/amp |url-status=dead }} However, Queally pulled out due to injury. (cancelled)\n|venue=[[Mohegan Sun Casino]]\n|attendance= \n|gate= \n|city=[[Uncasville, Connecticut]]\n}}\n\n'''Bellator 241: Pitbull vs. Carvalho''' was a scheduled event to take place on March 13, 2020 at [[Mohegan Sun Casino]] in [[Uncasville, Connecticut]]. The event was scheduled to be live on [[DAZN]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event was expected to feature a [[List of Bellator MMA champions#Featherweight World Championship|Bellator Featherweight World Championship]] bout between the champion [[Patr\u00edcio Freire]] and [[Pedro Carvalho (fighter)|Pedro Carvalho]].{{cite web |title=Patricio 'Pitbull' set to defend featherweight title against Pedro Carvalho at Bellator 241 |url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2020/1/9/21058799/patricio-pitbull-set-to-defend-featherweight-title-against-pedro-carvalho-at-bellator-241|website=mmafighting.com|date=January 9, 2020|author=Alexander K. Lee}}\n\nA heavyweight between former [[UFC Heavyweight Championship|UFC Heavyweight Champion]] [[Josh Barnett]] and [[Ronny Markes]] was expected for the event. The original meeting was scheduled for [[Bellator MMA in 2019|Bellator 235]], but Barnett was pulled out an hour before the fight due to illness and the fight was rebooked for this event.{{cite web |last1=Erickson |first1=Matt |title=Josh Barnett pulled from Bellator 235 main event vs. Ronny Markes |url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2019/12/josh-barnett-pulled-bellator-235-main-event-vs-ronny-markes-honolulu |website=[[MMAJunkie.com]] |access-date=5 March 2020 |date=20 December 2019}} Reports came out stating that Barnett was pulled due to a failed drug test, but Mike Mazzulli, head of the Mohegan Tribe Athletic Department, announced that the reports were false. However on March 4, it was announced that Barnett was officially off the card, which Mazzulli announced that a failed medical test was the reason for Barnett's removal and Bellator then announced that [[Matt Mitrione]] would replace Barnett against Markes.{{cite web |last1=Doyle |first1=David |title=Josh Barnett out, Matt Mitrione in vs. Ronny Markes at Bellator 241 |url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2020/03/josh-barnett-out-matt-mitrione-in-ronny-makes-bellator-241 |website=[[MMAJunkie.com]] |date=4 March 2020 |access-date=5 March 2020}}\n\nOn March 13, the day of the event, Bellator President Scott Coker announced that the event would be cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]].{{cite web|url=https://www.mmaweekly.com/bellator-makes-last-minute-decision-to-cancel-fridays-bellator-241-coronavirus-covid-19|title=Bellator makes last-minute decision to cancel Friday's Bellator The event was scheduled to be live on [[Channel 5 (British TV channel)|Channel 5]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event was expected to feature a bantamweight bout between rivals James Gallagher and Cal Ellenor.\n\nOn March 30, Bellator announced that the event would be cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]].\n\n'''Cancelled Fight card'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Bantamweight\n|James Gallagher\n|vs.\n|Cal Ellenor\n|\n|\n|\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent end|notes=yes}}\n\n==Bellator 243 (Cancelled)==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator 243: Carmouche vs. Bohm\n|image=\n|image_size=\n|date=May 29, 2020 (cancelled)\n|venue=[[Pechanga Resort and Casino]]\n|attendance= \n|gate= \n|city=[[Temecula, California]]\n}}\n\n'''Bellator 243: Carmouche vs. Bohm''' was a scheduled event to take place on May 29, 2020 at [[Pechanga Resort and Casino]] in [[Temecula, California]]. The event was scheduled to be live on [[Paramount Network]] and [[DAZN]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event was expected to feature a women's flyweight bout between former UFC title contender [[Liz Carmouche]] and Mandy Bohm.\n\nOn March 30, Bellator announced that the event would be cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]].\n\n'''Cancelled Fight card'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Women's Flyweight\n|[[Liz Carmouche]]\n|vs.\n|Mandy Bohm\n|\n|\n|\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent end|notes=yes}}\n\n==Bellator 244 (Cancelled)==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator 244: Chandler vs. Henderson 2\n|image=\n|image_size=\n|date=June 6, 2020 (cancelled)\n|venue=[[Wintrust Arena]]\n|attendance= \n|gate= \n|city=[[Chicago, Illinois]]\n}}\n\n'''Bellator 244: Chandler vs. Henderson 2''' was a scheduled event to take place on June 6, 2020 at [[Wintrust Arena]] in [[Chicago, Illinois]]. The event was scheduled to be live on [[DAZN]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event was expected to feature a rematch between former Bellator world champion [[Michael Chandler]] and former UFC and WEC world champion [[Benson Henderson]], with Chandler having won the first bout.\n\nAdditionally, a semi-final matchup in the [[#Bellator Featherweight World Grand Prix Tournament|Bellator Featherweight World Grand Prix]] between former bantamweight champ [[Darrion Caldwell]] and [[A.J. McKee]] was scheduled for the card.\n\nOn April 21, Bellator announced that the event would be cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]].{{cite web |title=Bellator 244 postponed as coronavirus pandemic grows|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2020/04/bellator-244-postponed-coronavirus-pandemic|date=April 21, 2020|author=Simon Samano}}\n\n'''Cancelled Fight card'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Fight card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Lightweight\n|[[Michael Chandler]]\n|vs.\n|[[Benson Henderson]]\n|\n|\n|\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Featherweight\n|[[Darrion Caldwell]]\n|vs.\n|[[A.J. McKee]]\n|\n|\n|\n|[[#Bellator Featherweight World Grand Prix Tournament|Bellator Featherweight World Grand Prix]] Semi-Final bout.}}\n{{MMAevent end|notes=yes}}\n\n==Bellator 242==\n\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator 242: Bandejas vs. Pettis\n|image=\n|image_size=\n|date= July 24, 2020\n|venue=[[Mohegan Sun Arena]] \n|attendance= None ([[behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]])\n|city=[[Uncasville, Connecticut]]\n}}\n\n'''Bellator 242: Bandejas vs. Pettis''' took place on July 24, 2020 at the [[Mohegan Sun Arena]] in [[Uncasville, Connecticut]].{{cite web|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2020/07/bellator-return-july-24-sergio-pettis-vs-ricky-bandejas-booked/amp?__twitter_impression=true|title=Bellator to return July 24; Sergio Pettis, Ricky Bandejas booked to fight|author=Raphael Marinho|publisher=mmajunkie.com|date=July 14, 2020}}\n\nThe event aired live on [[Paramount Network]] and [[DAZN]].\n\nBellator 242 marked the organization's return to live events following a shutdown due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and was held behind closed doors without fans in attendance.\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Main card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Bantamweight\n|[[Sergio Pettis]]\n|def.\n|Ricky Bandejas\n|Decision (unanimous) (30-27, 30-27, 30-27)\n|3\n|5:00\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Welterweight\n|[[Jason Jackson (fighter)|Jason Jackson]]\n|def.\n|[[Jordan Mein]]\n|Decision (unanimous) (30-27, 30-27, 30-27)\n|3\n|5:00\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Featherweight\n|Jay Jay Wilson\n|def.\n|[[Tywan Claxton]]\n|Decision (split) (27-30, 29-28, 30-27)\n|3\n|5:00\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Featherweight\n|[[Aaron Pico]]\n|def.\n|Solo Hatley Jr.\n|Submission (rear-naked choke)\n|1\n|2:10\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent card|Preliminary card|header=no}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Welterweight\n|Mark Lemminger\n|def.\n|Jake Smith\n|TKO (punches)\n|2\n|4:46\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Bantamweight\n|[[Raufeon Stots]]\n|def.\n|Cass Bell\n|Submission (rear-naked choke)\n|3\n|1:24\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Heavyweight\n|Ras Hylton\n|def.\n|Rudy Schaffroth\n|Decision (unanimous) (29-28, 29-28, 29-28)\n|3\n|5:00\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent end|notes=yes}}\n{{cite web |title=Bellator 242: Bandejas vs. Pettis|url=http://www.bellator.com/events/yxvea9/bellator-242-bandejas-vs-pettis |access-date=26 July 2020}}\n\n==Bellator 243==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator 243: Chandler vs. Henderson 2\n|image=\n|image_size=\n|date= August 7, 2020\n|venue=[[Mohegan Sun Arena]] \n|attendance= \n|gate= \n|city=[[Uncasville, Connecticut]]\n}}\n\n'''Chandler vs. Henderson 2''' was initially scheduled to take place at Bellator 244 on June 6, 2020 at [[Wintrust Arena]] in [[Chicago, Illinois]]. However, the event was postponed due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2020/4/21/21230011/bellator-244-postponed-over-covid-19-safety-concerns|title=Bellator 244 postponed over COVID-19 safety concerns|author=Steven Marrocco|publisher=mmafighting.com|date=April 21, 2020}} It was announced that the bout was rescheduled as the main event of Bellator 243 set to take place on August 7 from the [[Mohegan Sun Arena]] in [[Uncasville, Connecticut]].\n\nThe event aired live on [[Paramount Network]] and [[DAZN]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event featured a lightweight rematch between former three-time [[List of Bellator MMA champions#Lightweight World Championship|Bellator lightweight champion]] [[Michael Chandler]] and former [[List of World Extreme Cagefighting champions#Lightweight Championship|WEC]] and [[List of UFC champions#Lightweight Championship|UFC lightweight champion]] [[Benson Henderson]]. To set up for Bellator Lightweight Title contention.{{cite web |last1=Staff |first1=bellator.com |title=Bellator 244 |url=http://www.bellator.com/events/imwafl/bellator-244-chandler-vs-henderson-2 Bennett weighed in at 131.7 pounds, 5.7 pounds over the non-title flyweight limit of 126.0 pounds, and Diggs weighed in at 157 pounds, 1 pound over the non-title lightweight limit of 156 pounds. Both bouts proceeded at catchweights and both fighters were fined a percentage of their respective purses, a percentage that went to their opponents.{{cite Milan: Gallagher vs. Ellenor |access-date=15 September 2020}}\n\n==Bellator 248==\n{{Infobox MMA event\n|name=Bellator Paris/Bellator 248\n|image=\n|image_size=\n|date=October 10, 2020\n|venue=[[AccorHotels Arena]]\n|city=[[Paris, France]]\n}}\n\n'''Bellator Paris/Bellator 248''' was a mixed martial arts event scheduled for October 10, 2020 from [[Paris, France]]. It was the first major MMA event held in France since the sport was legalized back in January.\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThis was the first event where a leading MMA organization held a live event in front of a paying audience in France. One thousand tickets were made available and were all sold out within 48 hours.\n\nThe Bellator Paris portion of the card aired on [[Channel 5 (British TV channel)|Channel 5]] and featured a heavyweight bout between former title challenger [[Cheick Kongo]] and [[Timothy Johnson (fighter)|Timothy Johnson]]. The two previously met at [[Bellator MMA in 2018|Bellator 208]] where Kongo won by knockout the first round.\n\nThe Bellator 248 portion of the card aired on [[CBS Sports Network]] and featured a welterweight bout between [[Michael Page (fighter)|Michael Page]] and former [[Cage Warriors|Cage Warriors Welterweight Champion]] Ross Houston. The bout was later updated to a 175-pound catchweight contest.\n\n'''Results'''\n\n{{MMAevent}}\n{{MMAevent card|Bellator Paris card}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Heavyweight\n|[[Timothy Johnson (fighter)|Timothy Johnson]]\n|def.\n|[[Cheick Kongo]]\n|Decision (split) (28-29, 29-28, 29-28)\n|3\n|5:00\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Featherweight\n|Saul Rogers\n|def.\n|Arbi Mezhidov\n|Submission (rear-naked choke)\n|1\n|4:38\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent card|Bellator Paris Prelims|header=no}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Lightweight\n|Yves Landu\n|def.\n|Terry Brazier\n|KO (flying knee)\n|1\n|2:18\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Featherweight\n|Fabacary Diatta\n|def.\n|Dominique Wooding\n|Decision (unanimous) (29-28, 29-28, 30-27)\n|3\n|5:00\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Women's Flyweight\n|[[Lucie Bertaud]]\n|def.\n|Maguy Berchel\n|Decision (unanimous) (29-28, 30-26, 30-26)\n|3\n|5:00\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Featherweight\n|Ciran Clarke\n|def.\n|Jean N'Doye\n|Decision (unanimous) (30-26, 30-27, 30-27)\n|3\n|5:00\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent card|Bellator 248 card|header=no}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Catchweight (175 lb)\n|[[Michael Page (fighter)|Michael Page]]\n|def.\n|Ross Houston\n|Decision (unanimous) (29-28, 30-27, 30-27)\n|3\n|5:00\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Welterweight\n|[[Oliver Enkamp]]\n|def.\n|Emmanuel Dawa\n|Submission (japanese necktie)\n|1\n|4:10\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent bout\n|Catchweight (160 lb)\n|Alan Omer\n|def.\n|Ryan Scope\n|TKO (punches)\n|1\n|1:46\n|\n}} \n{{MMAevent bout\n|Featherweight\n|[[Mads Burnell]]\n|def.\n|Darko Banovic\n|TKO (punches)\n|1\n|3:13\n|\n}}\n{{MMAevent end|notes=yes}}\n{{cite web|url=http://www.bellator.com/events/jnmp1i/bellator-es-10-kongo-vs-johnson-ii|title=Bellator Paris: Jo go vs. Johnson 2 |access-date=11 September 2020}}

However, the bout was removed from the card when the Mohegan Tribal Athletic Commission deemed Freire unable to compete due to what was termed an undisclosed medical issue.{{cite This event aired live on [[CBS Sports Network]].\n\n'''Background'''\n\nThe event featured a Women's Flyweight main event for the [[List of Bellator champions#Women's Flyweight World Championship|Bellator Women's Flyweight World Championship]] between [[Ilima-Lei Macfarlane]] and [[Juliana Velasquez]].\n\nAt weigh ins, [[Goiti Yamauchi]] weighed in at 162.8 pounds, 6.8 pounds over the lightweight limit. The bout against [[Professional Fighters League|PFL]] veteran, Nate Andrews was cancelled. [[Mohegan Sun]] commission head, Mike Mazzulli, said that from now on Yamauchi will be required to fight at [[Welterweight (MMA)|Welterweight]], 170 pounds.{{Cite news|url=https://cagesidepress.com/2020/12/09/goiti-yamauchi-vs-nate-andrews-off-bellator-254-following-weigh-in/|title=Goiti Yamauchi vs. Nate Andrews Off Bellator 254 Following Weigh-In Flub|work=cagesidepress|access-date=2020-12-09}}\n\nA women's featherweight bout between [[Marina Mokhnatkina]] and [[Jessica Borga]] was scheduled for this event but cancelled a week before for unknown reasons.{{Cite news|url=https://mymmanews.com/marina-mokhnatkina-vs-jessica-borga-removed-from-bellator-254/|title=Marina Mokhnatkina vs. Jessica Borga removed from Bellator 254|work=mymmanews|access-date=2020-12-09}}\n\nThis would be the last card to air on CBS Sports Network; all Bellator cards will air exclusively on [[Showtime (TV network)|Showtime]] beginning in MMA|2022]]\n}}\n\n'''2021 in Bellator MMA''' was the thirteenth year in the history of [[Bellator MMA]], a [[mixed martial arts]] promotion based in the United States. Bellator held '''18 events''' in 2021.\n\n==Background==\nThe promotion went on a hiatus following Bellator 254 on December 10, 2020, which would be the final card to air on [[CBS Sports Network]].{{cite web|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2021/2/3/22265308/bellator-targets-april-9-for-2021-return-in-familiar-venue|title=Bellator targets April 9 for 2021 return in familiar venue|author=Steven Marrocco|date=February 3, 2021|publisher=mmafighting.com}} Beginning in April, Bellator's U.S broadcasts moved to the [[Pay television|premium]] [[Showtime (TV network)|Showtime]] network.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/mma/news/bellator-set-for-showtime-debut-in-april-as-star-studded-light-heavyweight-world-grand-prix-headlines-slate/amp/|title=Bellator set for Showtime debut in April as star-studded Light Heavyweight World Grand Prix headlines slate|work=CBS Sports|author=Brent Brookhouse|date=2021-02-09|accessdate=2021-02-09}} Bellator 255, which took place on April 2, 2021, was the promotion's debut on Showtime, and the first MMA card to air on the network in over eight years; the last event being [[Strikeforce: Marquardt vs. Saffiedine]] on They include current champion [[Sergio Pettis]], the former [[Rizin Fighting Federation|Rizin]] and Bellator champion [[Kyoji Horiguchi]], another former Bellator champion in [[Juan Archuleta]], who captured the vacant bantamweight title in 2020 against [[Patchy Mix]], who will also be in the tournament. The final four fighters in the Grand Prix are all ranked in the top six by Bellator at 135 pounds: [[Magomed Magomedov (fighter)|Magomed Magomedov]], James Gallagher, [[Raufeon Stots]] and [[Leandro Higo]].{{Cite web|last=Al-Shatti|first=Shaun|date=2021-12-03|title=Bellator announces $1 million bantamweight grand prix for 2022, eight-man tournament field|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2021/12/3/22816962/bellator-announces-1-million-bantamweight-grand-prix-for-2022-eight-man-tournament-field|access-date=2021-12-04|website=MMA The lineup includes [[Usman Nurmagomedov]], [[A.J. McKee]], [[Tofiq Musayev]], [[Alexandr Shabliy]], [[Patricky Freire]], [[Mansour Barnaoui]], [[Benson Henderson]], and [[Sidney Outlaw]]. The tournament kicked off at [[Bellator 292]] on March 10 in San Jose, California.{{Cite web |last=Sherdog.com |title=Eight-Man Field Announced for Bellator Lightweight Grand Prix |url=https://www.sherdog.com/news/news/EightMan-Field-Announced-for-Bellator-Lightweight-Grand-Prix-188898 |access-date=2023-01-11 |website=Sherdog |language=en}} \n\n{{#invoke:RoundN|main|columns=3|score-boxes=1|3rdplace=no\n|team-width=200\n|score-width=\n\n\n|| {{nowrap|{{flagicon|RUS}} '''[[Usman Nurmagomedov]] (c)'''}} | '''[[Bellator 292|SUB]]''' | {{flagicon|USA}} [[Benson Henderson]] | 1\n|| {{flagicon|FRA}} [[Mansour Barnaoui]] | [[Bellator 296|5]] | {{flagicon|USA}} '''[[Brent Primus]]'''{{efn|Primus replaced [[Sidney Outlaw]] after he was suspended for a positive drug test.}} | '''[[Bellator 296|UD]]''' \n|| {{flagicon|AZE}} [[Tofiq Musayev]] | 3 | {{flagicon|RUS}} '''[[Alexandr Shabliy]]''' | '''[[Bellator 292|TKO]]'''\n|| {{flagicon|BRA}} [[Roberto de Souza]]{{efn|de Souza replaced [[A. [[2024 in Professional Fighters League|2024 in PFL]]\n| followed_by = [[2026 in Professional Fighters League|2026 in PFL]]\n}}\n\nThe year '''2025''' was the 7th year in the history of the [[Professional Fighters League]] (PFL), a [[mixed martial arts]] promotion based in the United States.\n\n==Background==\nOn January 7, 2025, PFL chairman [[Donn Davis]] announced that elbows will be legal in the promotion, after the PFL had banned elbows for the regular season and playoffs. Elbows were typically allowed in non-season and non-playoff fights only.{{Cite web |date=2025-01-07 |title=Donn Davis announces that elbows now legal in all PFL bouts \n|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2025/01/pfl-elbows-legal-all-fights |access-date=2025-01-15 |website=MMA Junkie |language=en-US}}\n\nOn January 9, 2025, it was announced that the 2025 season of PFL would no longer operate as a points-based tournament, but would rather be contested as a single-elimination tournament.{{Cite web |date=2025-01-09 |title=PFL ditches $1 million winner, season points format for 2025 \n|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2025/01/pfl-changes-1-million-winner-season-points-format-2025-mma |access-date=2025-01-15 |website=MMA Junkie |language=en-US}}\n\nOn January 15, 2025, PFL revealed that hold eight tournaments in 2025, confirming the $500,000 pay for each winner. In total, it will distribute more than $20 million to the fighters. The tournaments will take place at heavyweight, light heavyweight, middleweight, welterweight, lightweight, featherweight, bantamweight and women's flyweight divisions.{{Cite web |last=Cruz |first=Guilherme |date=2025-01-15 |title=PFL reveals dates, details for new tournament format in 2025 \n|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2025/1/15/24344310/pfl-reveals-dates-details-new-tournament-format-2025 |access-date=2025-01-15 |website=MMA Fighting |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2025-01-15 |title=PFL announces 2025 tournaments over eight weight classes with fighters TBD \n|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2025/01/pfl-2025-tournaments-eight-weight-classes |access-date=2025-01-15 |website=MMA Junkie |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Holland |first=Jesse |date=2025-01-15 |title=New-look PFL announces 2025 World Tournament, start date and weight brackets \n|url=https://www.mmamania.com/2025/1/15/24344326/new-look-pfl-announces-2025-world-tournament-start-date-weight-brackets-mma |access-date=2025-01-15 |website=MMAmania.com |language=en}}\n\n==Events
